campaign_platform_points: Jobs & labor: Garamendi positions himself as the leading congressional voice for 'Make It In America' policies to bring manufacturing jobs back to the U.S., including raising Buy America requirements for rail and buses, extending wind and solar tax credits, and increasing American shipbuilding.

Environment & climate: Garamendi opposes the proposed $15 billion twin tunnels through the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, arguing they would drain the Delta dry six months a year. He advocates for surface storage (Sites Reservoir), levee repairs, and water infrastructure investment instead.

Healthcare: Garamendi supports a national public option to increase competition, importing prescription drugs from countries with rigorous safety standards, allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices directly, incentivizing rural hospitals and clinics, and faster student loan forgiveness for primary care physicians in underserved areas.

Education: Garamendi opposes cuts to all levels of education, advocates for lower class sizes, preservation of after-school and arts programs, federal STEM investment, and a Student Loan Refinancing Act to lower interest rates for all borrowers to 3.23%.

Transportation: Garamendi advocates robust federal investment in roads, bridges, ports, levees, and transit systems; supports the Capitol Corridor and regional bus systems; fights for bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure; and pushes Make It In America standards for federally funded transportation equipment.

Other: Garamendi is resolutely opposed to privatizing Social Security, dismantling Medicare, or defunding Medicaid/MediCal. He urges Congress to allow drug importation, Medicare price negotiation, and expansion of Medicare to include dental and vision coverage for seniors.

Other: Garamendi advocates reducing the VA claims backlog, reforming duplicative civilian credentialing for veterans, and an improved 21st-century GI Bill with dramatically increased funding for educational benefits, trade and technical training, veterans' housing, and entrepreneurial opportunities.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Garamendi supports full LGBT equality including marriage equality and the Equality Act, calls for restoring the Voting Rights Act, opposes voter suppression tactics, supports religious freedom protections, and backs the Women's Economic Initiative including paid sick leave and equal pay.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Josh pledges to cut the cost of prescription drugs like insulin, repeal gas taxes at both the federal and state level, and bring housing costs under control to make the Valley affordable for families.
Healthcare: Josh supports capping insulin at $35 per month and working to bring more doctors to the Central Valley so residents can access affordable care closer to home.

Criminal justice & public safety: Josh commits to funding law enforcement with federal dollars to fight methamphetamine and fentanyl trafficking, hire new police officers, purchase police vehicles, and equip departments with modern public safety technology.

Jobs & labor: Josh aims to bring high-paying jobs in ag-tech, IT, and clean energy to the Central Valley and supports trade deals that prioritize American products and workers over foreign competitors.

Homelessness: Josh declares homelessness an emergency and supports urgent programs to get people into support services, investing in mental health and substance abuse treatment plus job training to address root causes.

Government accountability & ethics: Josh authored the Ban Corporate PACs Act, opposes pay raises and special privileges for politicians, and advocates campaign finance reform so elected officials serve families rather than corporations.

Immigration: Josh co-sponsors the DREAM Act to provide a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers, advocates comprehensive immigration reform for immigrant protections, and supports strong border security and enhanced technology.

Environment & climate: Josh opposes the Delta Tunnel project that would divert Valley water to Los Angeles, supports bipartisan water storage projects, and introduced the FARM Act to help farmers address climate change.

campaign_platform_points: Jobs & labor: DeSaulnier advocates for workers to have a voice as AI and automation reshape the economy. He supports protecting the right to organize, safe workplaces, living wages, and has authored legislation to tax excessive CEO pay and protect workers from mass layoffs.

Housing: DeSaulnier prioritizes expanding affordable housing and reducing housing costs through transit-oriented development, federal investments, and research on telework to reduce congestion. He previously created a permanent funding source for affordable housing as a State Senator.

Environment & climate: DeSaulnier fights to protect California's vehicle emission standards and clean energy investments against federal rollbacks. He advocates for Delta water protection, fossil fuel worker transition programs, and opposes attempts to undermine federal land protections.

Government accountability & ethics: DeSaulnier positions himself as the top Democrat on the House Ethics Committee, holding Congress to higher standards. He emphasizes transparency through over 260 town halls and ensuring constituents have direct access to their representative and answers.

Healthcare: DeSaulnier fights to protect NIH and medical research funding, having been personally saved by federally funded cancer research. He advocates for expanding access to quality care and improving patient navigation through the healthcare system after a diagnosis.

Criminal justice & public safety: DeSaulnier supports evidence-based gun violence reduction, including funding research on what works, investing in gun safety technology, and enabling communities to share effective local strategies. He supported the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: DeSaulnier fights to codify reproductive rights into federal law, opposing any federal legislation that would restrict women's access to healthcare or override California's protections. He also sponsors legislation on contraception and IVF access.

Immigration: DeSaulnier pushes for humane, fair, and functional immigration reform. He opposes mass deportation policies, demands accountability for ICE actions, and advocates for dignity for families already living and contributing in the community.

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Lateefah will champion legislation closing loopholes in federal gun laws, stopping illegal firearms flow into communities, and providing resources for mental health, addiction treatment, and recidivism prevention programs. She also advocates progressive policing models like non-sworn transit ambassadors and crisis intervention specialists.

Housing: Housing is framed as a fundamental right. Lateefah will pursue $4.5 billion for permanent supportive housing, expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, increase rental subsidies, end landlord discrimination, and support building 3 million homes over four years with first-time buyer assistance.

Homelessness: Lateefah will leverage federal funds to convert empty government buildings into dignified emergency shelters, build more transitional housing units in the East Bay, and increase federal aid for mental health and social worker staffing at the frontlines of the homelessness crisis.

Economy & cost of living: Lateefah supports a living wage, aid to small businesses, infrastructure investment for job creation, banning corporate price-gouging to lower grocery prices, and ensuring the wealthiest Americans and corporations pay their fair share to reduce income inequality.

Healthcare: Lateefah advocates for a public option and ultimately an affordable single-payer health system. She will expand Medicare drug price negotiation to all drugs, close the Medicaid coverage gap, expand Medicare to dental/vision/hearing, lower the Medicare eligibility age, and invest in maternal and infant mortality reduction.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Lateefah will fight to restore and protect a woman's right to choose, guaranteeing safe and legal abortion access for every woman regardless of location or income. She will push back against every effort to strip away reproductive rights.

Criminal justice & public safety: Lateefah will support legislation to prohibit the federal death penalty and require re-sentencing of those currently on death row. She draws on her experience creating the Back on Track anti-recidivism program and her work empowering survivors of trafficking and violence.

Immigration: Lateefah will work to create a fair and humane immigration system that disentangles the criminal system from immigration, expands legal pathways to work authorization and citizenship, defends DACA, and ensures Dreamers have a pathway to citizenship and access to the social safety net.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Sam Liccardo prioritizes accelerating construction of affordable and market-rate housing through bipartisan legislation, cutting red tape, modernizing reviews, and converting vacant office buildings into housing. He authored five bipartisan housing bills, four of which passed both chambers.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign centers on reducing the cost of living for working families, including lowering bank and financial transaction fees, eliminating cost-inflating tariffs, and reducing health insurance premiums through bipartisan legislation.

Healthcare: Liccardo introduced the Fix It Act, a bipartisan ACA premium tax credit extension designed to lower health insurance premiums for 22 million Americans while saving taxpayer dollars, securing cosponsors from both parties to break a legislative stalemate.

Jobs & labor: Through Innovation for Good and the Innovation Agenda, Liccardo advocates a pro-innovation framework to keep America competitive in AI and advanced manufacturing, retain skilled international talent, and prepare workers for AI-driven industries through employer-college partnerships.

Environment & climate: Liccardo established the Wildfire Resilience Partnership and the Partnership for the Coastside's Future to coordinate wildfire prevention, coastal resilience, and infrastructure investment. He also advanced efforts to reduce wildfire-related property insurance costs through fire safety investments.

Government accountability & ethics: Liccardo authored the MEME Act to ban elected officials from profiting off cryptocurrency schemes, the POCCA Act to prevent unconstitutional withholding of appropriated funds, and the SUN Act to address unlawful military deployments in American cities.

Homelessness: Liccardo led opposition to federal Continuum of Care changes that would have pushed extremely low-income families into homelessness and secured federal funding for local affordable housing and homelessness reduction projects throughout the district.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: The campaign states advocacy for voting rights, reproductive freedom, and protection of Social Security, Medi-Cal, and CalFresh funding, while opposing cuts to healthcare and food assistance programs impacting working families and seniors.

campaign_platform_points: Immigration: Zoe Lofgren positions herself as a champion of comprehensive, top-to-bottom immigration reform and a staunch defender of the DACA program, drawing on her background as an immigration attorney and law professor.

Other: As Ranking Member of the House Science, Space and Technology Committee, Lofgren plans to push Congress and the Administration to accelerate fusion energy research, spur innovation in agriculture, and cultivate the nation's STEM pipeline.

Environment & climate: Lofgren states she will work to bolster the federal scientific agenda on wildfires and flooding, framing these as yearly seasonal climate issues causing increasing devastation to California communities.

Government accountability & ethics: Lofgren identifies as a longtime leader on anti-corruption, campaign finance, and pro-democracy reforms, having shepherded the For the People Act to limit big money in politics, make voting easier, and ensure politicians serve the public interest.

Housing: Lofgren states she has been committed to solving the affordable housing crisis in the San Jose area for decades, a commitment that began when she was first Executive Director of a local community housing non-profit.

Government accountability & ethics: Lofgren highlights her role in passing the bipartisan Presidential Election Reform Act as part of her work on election integrity and protecting the democratic process following the January 6th Capitol attack.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Proposes multiple bills: tying Title I funds to measurable 10% proficiency gains, mandatory civics education grades 3–12, financial literacy graduation requirements, school-business workforce partnerships, and funding tied directly to students to increase parental choice and school accountability.

Immigration: Supports modernized H-2A agricultural visa with vetting, English instruction, and financial literacy training; federal-local partnerships for case processing; and counting only U.S. citizens for congressional apportionment and Census-derived federal funding allocations.

Economy & cost of living: Proposes a 7% flat tax on wages and salaries (cutting liability ~50%), full deductions for gym memberships, sports leagues, and wellness training, 2% annual deficit reduction paired with 4% GDP growth targets, and aggressive reshoring of key industries.

Environment & climate: Advocates an all-of-the-above energy strategy: continued clean-tech investment, responsible use of domestic natural gas as a bridge fuel, expanded clean hydrogen, next-generation hydroelectric with mag-lev transmission, and reducing emissions through technology rather than mandates.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: The campaign's central mission is restoring affordability to California. Verbica pledges to end high gas taxes and reformulated fuel blends, lower food costs by providing water for farmers, and bypass Sacramento on state income and sales taxes using a strategy modeled on Prop 13 for property taxes. He also advocates conservative central bank policy to combat inflation and currency debasement.

Housing: Verbica supports giving neighborhoods autonomy over local housing decisions, positioning this as a key component of restoring affordability. The campaign also links housing costs to CEQA regulation, referencing the California Policy Center's critique that CEQA is the centerpiece of California's skyrocketing home prices.

Immigration: Verbica calls for immigration reform specifically framed to benefit California's technology and agricultural sectors, while also advocating for the sanctity of the nation's borders. He supports interagency law enforcement cooperation on immigration enforcement.

Criminal justice & public safety: Verbica highlights the fentanyl and synthetic opioid epidemic as a devastating crisis killing tens of thousands of young Americans annually. He specifically addresses China's regulatory and enforcement failures in the international networks that sustain the fentanyl supply chain.

Jobs & labor: Verbica pledges to stop PAGA's assault on California businesses and end the assault on independent contractors. He frames over-regulation of business as a key concern for constituents and positions himself as pro-business and pro-agriculture.

Government accountability & ethics: Verbica supports the California Voter ID initiative for the 2026 ballot and calls for stopping the epidemic of billions in unfunded liabilities in local counties and cities. He advocates transparency, accountability, and small government as core principles.

Healthcare: Verbica identifies the California insurance crisis as a priority to fix, arguing that Democrats have made healthcare more expensive for middle-class Californians. He frames lowering insurance rates as part of the broader affordability agenda.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Chew pledges to introduce comprehensive debt reduction legislation in his first year, combining spending restraint, entitlement reform, tax base broadening, and dedicated debt-reduction revenues. He also supports honest budgeting requiring 10/20/30-year cost analysis and building a bipartisan fiscal coalition.

Other: Chew argues Social Security and Medicare face bankruptcy within years and demands reform within six years. He lists over a dozen specific proposals including raising retirement age, increasing payroll tax, reducing high-earner benefits, and taxing Social Security benefits, emphasizing no pain-free solution exists.

Healthcare: Chew acknowledges no magic solution exists and criticizes politicians who claim otherwise. He calls for a practical, honest conversation about delivering better care at lower cost while preserving innovation and quality, drawing on his 35 years managing health insurance across multiple countries.

Immigration: Chew advocates removing violent criminals and cartel traffickers while opposing use of limited government resources to pursue peaceful immigrants who contribute to the economy. He frames it as a common-sense distinction: deporting a drug kingpin makes communities safer; deporting a farm hand makes them poorer.

Education: Chew supports school choice empowering families to select schools meeting their children's needs with financial support. He opposes politicized ideological agendas in schools, advocates local control over federal bureaucratic dictates, and emphasizes teaching critical thinking and workforce-relevant skills.

Environment & climate: Chew supports an all-of-above energy strategy with heavy reliance on nuclear power, citing his nuclear submarine service. He specifically advocates investing in small modular reactors and argues wind and solar alone cannot meet energy demands from data centers, cloud computing, and AI.

International affairs: Chew supports Ukraine against Russia, countering China's military ambitions, maintaining Middle East stability, and watching North Korea and Iran. He criticizes Trump's unilateral Iran war as reckless, arguing it emboldened Iranian extremists and collapsed American strategic influence.

Housing: Chew frames Colorado's housing crisis as supply-and-demand, exacerbated by high mortgage rates linked to national debt, tariffs, immigration restrictions, and overbearing environmental regulations. His solution: tame deficits, reduce tariffs, welcome immigration labor, and repeal costly regulations.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: Hickenlooper refuses corporate PAC money, supports overturning Citizens United, champions stricter political money regulations and disclosures, fights government corruption, and works to protect voting access including universal vote-by-mail against suppression efforts.

Economy & cost of living: Hickenlooper demands the president pay back illegal tariff-taxes, fights to lower prices on groceries and medical care, and works to build an economy providing affordable housing, good-paying jobs, fair working conditions, and strong small businesses for all Coloradans.

Jobs & labor: Hickenlooper co-sponsors the PRO Act to strengthen workers' rights, supports labor unions and collective bargaining, authored legislation to prepare the workforce for AI, and champions apprenticeship programs and expanded access to capital for small businesses.

Immigration: Hickenlooper calls for ICE to be completely overhauled or shut down, voted against additional ICE funding, introduced legislation to ban masked agents and raids at schools, hospitals, and polling places, and works to protect Coloradans from mass deportation.

Criminal justice & public safety: Hickenlooper supports expanding background checks to all gun sales, banning assault weapons, and regulating safe home storage of firearms. As governor he passed sweeping gun safety reform including universal background checks and high-capacity magazine limits.

Environment & climate: Hickenlooper opposes selling public lands, protects NCAR funding, secured major climate and clean energy investment, created the Senate Colorado River Caucus, and as governor protected 100,000 acres of Colorado public lands and created gold-standard methane regulations.

Healthcare: Hickenlooper supports a public option, empowering Medicare to negotiate all drug prices, restoring Medicaid and ACA funding, improving access for rural and low-income communities, and creating transparency in health care costs to protect people from hidden prices.

Housing: Hickenlooper works to lower housing costs by preventing large corporations from dominating the housing market, cutting red tape that slows new home construction, and supporting local communities to invest in the housing they need.

campaign_platform_points: Jobs & labor: His stated first priority is raising pay for all workers and tying it to the Consumer Price Index. He also supports a federal minimum wage pegged to CPI, tax credits for employers who raise workers above subsidized-living levels, and opening a conversation on Universal Basic Income.

Environment & climate: Declares fossil fuels obsolete and calls for a smooth transition to clean energy starting now. Supports increasing and making permanent the solar tax credit, restoring rebates, banning net-metering offset caps so homeowners can sell excess power, and creating incentives for domestic solar-panel manufacturing.

Healthcare: Calls for reimagining the healthcare system so it works for everyone, noting healthcare for all would cost less than half the defense budget. Supports allowing midwives to bill Medicaid and private insurers for home births, and expanding FDA evaluation of natural herbal medicines to lower prescription drug costs.

Israel / Palestine: Calls for an immediate stop to U.S. weapons transfers to Israel, arguing self-defense does not justify killing or annexing sovereign neighbors. Supports the two-state solution based on pre-1967 borders as the best available path to peace and recognition.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Restore residential homeownership to American families by curbing corporate landlords and hedge funds, restoring affordability, and reviving small-town pathways to ownership and homesteading. Opposes the renter trap and perpetual debt to interest.

Immigration: Advocates common-sense immigration reform: a strong border, a functioning door, and a lean, clean, compassionate process that integrates good workers into the economy while eliminating the dysfunction that fuels corruption and cruelty.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: End mass surveillance by both corporations and government agencies. Establish comprehensive data privacy rights, require explicit informed consent for data collection, treat personal data as private property, and hold violators accountable. Proposes a Freedom From Surveillance Act.

Economy & cost of living: Build a people-centered economy that measures human thriving rather than Wall Street profit margins. Strengthen small businesses, cooperatives, and local supply chains. Fight predatory lending, reform medical and student debt, and reward savings and asset ownership.

Environment & climate: Protect public lands and ensure hunting, fishing, and hiking access for future generations. Champion restoration of watersheds, forests, and grasslands. Shift food supply from global to local, support regenerative practices, and invest in regenerative energy for food and energy independence.

Government accountability & ethics: Overturn Citizens United, reform campaign finance, and restore transparency to end corporate stranglehold on government. Eliminate federal overreach, empower local leadership, return authority to states and communities, and cut red tape and bureaucracy.

Education: Fully fund public education without pitting public school families against homeschool families. Bring back trades, arts, civics, financial literacy, and media literacy. Launch a national initiative to put working gardens and greenhouses in every public school.

Healthcare: Basic health care is a question of human decency. Supports food security (SNAP) as national security, improves VA access and mental health support for veterans and first responders, and combines compassion with Housing First, job training, and rehabilitation for the vulnerable.

Healthcare: Ashley Hinson supports lowering prescription drug costs through transparency and holding pharmacy benefit managers accountable, strengthening rural healthcare access, expanding maternal healthcare, supporting cancer research, and expanding over-the-counter birth control access.

Other: Ashley Hinson advocates protecting Iowa family farms from burdensome regulations, fighting California's Proposition 12, expanding export markets, passing a Farm Bill, and championing year-round E15 and biofuels to keep Iowa at the forefront of American energy.

Immigration: Ashley Hinson supports securing the southern border by enforcing America's immigration laws and deporting dangerous criminal illegal immigrants, framing border security as essential to protecting Iowa families.

Government accountability & ethics: Ashley Hinson proposes banning Members of Congress from trading individual stocks and betting on prediction markets, enacting lobbying bans, moving government agencies out of DC closer to the people, and rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse of tax dollars.

Parental rights in schools: Ashley Hinson supports giving families a stronger voice in their children's education and increasing school transparency, specifically pushing back on policies that allow students to secretly change their gender identity at school.

International affairs: Ashley Hinson calls for holding China accountable for stealing American jobs and innovation, purchasing American farmland, and engaging in unfair trade practices that hurt Iowa farmers, workers, and businesses.

Criminal justice & public safety: Ashley Hinson supports combating fentanyl and violent crime by cracking down on traffickers, strengthening partnerships with law enforcement, and holding violent offenders accountable to keep Iowa communities safe.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: The campaign supports making Roe v. Wade federal law, protecting access to contraception and IVF, defending freedom of speech and protest, protecting the right to marry who you love, and reforming the path to legal citizenship.

Education: The campaign opposes school vouchers, supports restoring Department of Education funding, increasing public school funding so every child has access to a world-class education, and protecting funding for Iowa Area Education Agencies.

Environment & climate: The campaign identifies Iowa's water quality crisis as the root cause of a cancer crisis, pledging to fund water quality sensors, crack down on chemical polluters, restore NIH and cancer research funding, and prohibit insurance denial of medically necessary cancer care.

Immigration: The campaign supports bipartisan immigration legislation that secures borders while simplifying an earned pathway to citizenship, stopping fentanyl at the border, and ensuring regulation and accountability for ICE agents.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: Laehn pledges to sponsor legislation eliminating the role of PACs and super PACs in elections, arguing both parties concentrate power and serve monied elites rather than the people they represent.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Laehn will seek legislation to prohibit private companies from using the state's eminent domain power to seize property for commercial gain, citing the 2005 Supreme Court decision as an error.

Government accountability & ethics: Laehn will work to restore the constitutional separation of powers among the three branches, specifically returning legislative authority to Congress and curbing unilateral presidential lawmaking via executive orders.

Economy & cost of living: Laehn will vote against any funding measure that increases the national debt except in extreme national emergency, and will fight for a constitutional balanced-budget amendment to constrain Congress.

Immigration: Laehn supports a secure border while simultaneously advocating to raise or eliminate artificial caps on legal immigration, arguing the two goals are not mutually exclusive and both parties should acknowledge this.

Other: Laehn states Congress should have no role in regulating abortion and will work to uphold the Dobbs decision, treating abortion policy as a matter reserved for the states under the Constitution.

Criminal justice & public safety: Laehn says the very first bill he will introduce in the Senate is to decriminalize the possession and use of marijuana, citing his experience as a prosecutor showing drug laws do more harm than good.

Criminal justice & public safety: Barr strongly supports police, opposes defunding and cashless bail, and has secured DOJ/COPS grants, expanded HIDTA designations, and passed the Thin Blue Line Act and Protect and Serve Act to strengthen penalties for assaulting officers.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: Proposes the Clean Hands Act: constitutional term limits (3 House, 2 Senate terms), ban on stock/crypto/commodities trading by Congress, lifetime lobbying ban, 5-year revolving-door ban for agency officials, single-issue bills, 72-hour bill text disclosure, no pay without a passed budget, dark money transparency, and mandatory 10-year tax return disclosure.

Other: Calls for a national AI standard requiring any AI in live video or voice to identify itself, banning AI impersonation without consent, prohibiting companion AI for minors, requiring banks to flag unusual transfers to protect seniors, and holding companies accountable for deploying undisclosed human-passing AI.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Supports federal standards governing AI-powered surveillance systems like Flock: purge unmatched footage within days, prohibit searchable location databases, restrict real-time alerts to violent felonies and active warrants, require court orders for historical searches, ban data sale to private entities, and mandate public annual reporting.

Other: Protects current and near-retirement Social Security benefits unchanged, opposes taxing benefits, proposes raising the wage cap for payroll taxes, gradually raising the retirement age for future workers only, and growing the workforce through economic policy to ensure long-term trust fund solvency.

Healthcare: Fights to break up vertically integrated insurance conglomerates and PBM monopolies, lower prescription drug costs, expand telehealth access, and require full transparency in drug pricing including clear upfront disclosure of the difference between cash price and insurance price for the same prescription.

Housing: Supports permitting reform with real deadlines for local and state approval, opposes green-energy mandates that force builders to absorb costs passed to buyers, and explores real estate tokenization using blockchain-based ownership structures to let families buy fractional property stakes.

Environment & climate: Supports an all-of-the-above energy transition including solar, wind, geothermal, hydro, and nuclear power with small modular reactors, opposes Green New Deal mandates, supports amending the Jones Act to reduce LNG shipping costs, and long-term investment in fusion as clean baseload power.

Immigration: Supports securing the border, ending catch-and-release, reforming the asylum process, expanding legal immigration, and a targeted earned pathway to legal status and citizenship for DACA recipients and Dreamers who meet rigorous standards, while rejecting both blanket amnesty and mass deportation.

Immigration: The campaign supports enforcing immigration laws, deporting criminal illegal aliens, securing the border, and fighting efforts to abolish ICE or reopen America's borders. It also ties fraud convictions to mandatory deportation.
Economy & cost of living: The campaign opposes any tax increase on the middle class, supports protecting the Working Family Tax Cuts, and calls for Congress to spend less, borrow less, and tax less.

Healthcare: The campaign pledges to cut prescription drug costs, fight government and corporate bureaucrats and middlemen, and keep healthcare decisions in the hands of patients rather than faceless institutions.
Environment & climate: The campaign supports an all-of-the-above energy approach, backing all U.S. energy sources to lower utility bills and gas prices while continuing to protect the environment.
Parental rights in schools: The campaign pledges to keep men out of women's sports and locker rooms, framing this as protecting Minnesota kids from radical social experiments and insane ideologies.
Education: The campaign calls for education reform that restores parents' say in schools, increases transparency and accountability, and reverses the decline in student test scores.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Peggy Flanagan is running for Senate to fight back against Donald Trump and Elon Musk's cuts to public assistance programs that make it harder for families to get by, framing the race as a defense of working families against billionaire-driven government.

Healthcare: The campaign highlights Medicaid as a critical program that helped Flanagan's family and positions her as a defender of Medicaid against proposed federal cuts, signaling she will fight to protect access to healthcare for Minnesotans.

Housing: The campaign identifies Section 8 housing as a public program that helped Flanagan's family and that she will defend against federal cuts, positioning housing assistance as a core issue she will fight for in the Senate.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: As Lieutenant Governor, Flanagan is described as leading the fight to keep abortion legal in Minnesota, and the campaign presents this as an ongoing priority she will carry into the U.S. Senate.

Education: The campaign states Flanagan fought to ensure children of all backgrounds can access a high-quality education, and as Lt. Governor she made investments in education, signaling continued commitment to equitable schooling.

Jobs & labor: The campaign highlights Flanagan's role in co-chairing the Raise the Wage Coalition that successfully pushed to raise Minnesota's minimum wage for the first time in a decade, signaling her commitment to workers' wages.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign explicitly states that Flanagan will not accept money from corporate PACs, framing her campaign as people-powered and free from corporate influence in Washington.

Government accountability & ethics: Ban corporate PAC money and dark money in elections, reverse Citizens United, require donor disclosure, ban stock trading for elected officials, ban lobbying by former officials, and reform the Supreme Court.

campaign_platform_points: Immigration: Cindy Hyde-Smith supports ending illegal immigration, building a wall on the southwestern border, and increasing funding to enforce U.S. immigration laws. She states immigrants must enter the country by following the law.

Other: Hyde-Smith holds that all children including the unborn have a right to life, opposes taxpayer funding of abortions, and commits to voting to confirm pro-life judges who interpret the law as written rather than legislate from the bench.
Other: As an enhanced-carry permit holder and firearms owner, Hyde-Smith pledges to always stand up for Second Amendment constitutional rights, including the right to keep and bear arms.

Economy & cost of living: Hyde-Smith positions herself as a champion of Mississippi's agricultural economy, securing USDA purchases of catfish and shrimp, emergency commodity assistance for farmers, and phosphate on the Critical Minerals List to steady fertilizer supply.

Environment & climate: Hyde-Smith highlights her role in advancing the Yazoo Backwater flood management plan, securing Army Corps funding for pumps, levee mitigation, and dam repairs to protect Mississippi communities from flooding.

Other: Hyde-Smith promotes rural broadband expansion in Mississippi, including USDA ReConnect fiber grants for underserved counties and a bipartisan bill to reauthorize USDA middle-mile broadband funding through 2031.

Other: Hyde-Smith supports military installations and veterans in Mississippi, voting for the PACT Act to expand VA care for burn-pit-exposed veterans and directing construction funding to Camp Shelby, Keesler AFB, and Columbus AFB.

Criminal justice & public safety: Hyde-Smith highlights co-sponsoring the HALT Fentanyl Act, which permanently schedules fentanyl analogues as Schedule I controlled substances, as a key public safety achievement of her Senate tenure.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Ricketts positions agriculture as the backbone of Nebraska's economy, supports biofuels like ethanol, crop insurance, voluntary conservation programs, foreign market access for producers, and opposes burdensome federal regulations such as the 30×30 plan and expanded Waters of the U.S. rules.

Government accountability & ethics: Ricketts argues reckless federal spending has created a crippling national debt and calls for common-sense spending control, elimination of bureaucratic red tape, fixing federal agency dysfunction, and restoring regular order to the congressional appropriations process.

Immigration: Ricketts supports building the border wall, reforming asylum laws, increasing federal penalties for fentanyl distributors, stopping sanctuary cities, and giving Border Patrol agents tools to control illegal immigration and keep drugs off streets.

Environment & climate: Ricketts advocates responsible use of natural resources, supports year-round E15 ethanol, biodiesel, sustainable aviation fuel, and nuclear energy, while opposing expanded WOTUS definitions and emissions mandates that would force a mass transition to electric vehicles.

Parental rights in schools: Ricketts supports taking the federal government out of the classroom, localized education with parental control at the forefront, and school choice at both state and federal levels. He also supports banning federal taxpayer funding for abortions.

Other: Ricketts supports cutting federal taxes on military retirement pay, promoting veteran hiring in public and private sectors, the Major Richard Star Act for combat-injured veterans, and increasing access to mental health and suicide prevention services.

Economy & cost of living: Ricketts introduced the Social Security Check Tax Cut Act to phase out the federal tax on Social Security income, supports protecting seniors' healthcare access, and is working to combat fraud and identity theft targeting older Americans.

International affairs: Ricketts supports stronger defense investments, modernizing America's nuclear deterrent including the Sentinel ICBM system, and pushing back against Chinese Communist Party aggression on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to protect American sovereignty.

antisemitism_education_policy_evidence.summary: Named as a cosponsor of the 2025 Antisemitism Awareness Act in Senator Tim Scott’s February 12 introduction announcement; it directs the Education Department to use IHRA’s definition for campus investigations.

He takes no corporate PAC money.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign's Tax Cuts and Lower Costs Blueprint targets utility bills, grocery prices, child-care costs, and housing. Pappas opposes Trump tariffs on food, supports rolling back tariffs on everyday essentials, cracking down on AI-driven price discrimination, and protecting nutrition-assistance programs.

Housing: Pappas says he will take on Wall Street and private-equity firms driving up housing costs, cut red tape to build more housing, support first-time homebuyers, and push for a VA foreclosure moratorium so veterans do not lose their homes.

Environment & climate: Pappas fights to lower energy costs by cutting energy taxes, protecting LIHEAP heating assistance, lowering utility bills for veterans and military families, defending clean-energy tax credits, and working with Senator Mark Kelly to suspend the federal gas tax.

Economy & cost of living: Pappas pledges to lower costs for families and small businesses on utilities, groceries, child care, and housing; restore the expanded Child Tax Credit; protect New Hampshire from Trump tariffs; and provide tax cuts to reduce energy bills.

Healthcare: Pappas supports expanding Medicaid, restoring ACA enhanced premium tax credits, allowing Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices, capping insulin at $35, and limiting out-of-pocket costs for seniors.

Education: Pappas commits to investing in public schools, increasing Pell grants, making community college affordable, providing debt forgiveness for nursing students, and strengthening career training and apprenticeship programs.

Environment & climate: Pappas supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy, clean energy investment, EV charging infrastructure, climate resilience funding, replacing lead pipes, and addressing PFAS contamination with stronger national safety standards.

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Cory helped write and pass the First Step Act, a bipartisan bill making meaningful reforms to the criminal justice system and beginning to reverse the injustices of mass incarceration.

Economy & cost of living: His American Opportunity Accounts Act (baby bonds) would fund a federally-backed savings account for every child born in America, growing with them, to virtually close the racial wealth gap and ensure upward mobility for all.

Environment & climate: Cory's Environmental Justice Act strengthens legal protections against environmental injustice for communities of color, low-income communities, and indigenous communities. He is committed to addressing climate change with focus on vulnerable communities.
Healthcare: Cory has advocated to expand access to health care to every American as part of his commitment to equal justice and opportunity.

campaign_platform_points: Healthcare: Luján states that access to quality and affordable health care is a human right. He has championed expanding CHIP, strengthening Medicaid and Medicare, protecting patients with pre-existing conditions, and reauthorizing addiction treatment programs for pregnant and postpartum women.

Environment & climate: Luján positions himself as a champion of climate action and environmental justice. He has pushed to protect Chaco Canyon from oil and gas drilling, plug abandoned and orphaned wells, deploy carbon capture technologies, and build a clean energy economy.

Economy & cost of living: Luján has fought to raise the minimum wage, close the gender pay gap, expand rural broadband, and uplift the middle class. He secured funding for the Affordable Connectivity Program and the Savvy Savers Act to lower costs for families.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Husted positions himself as a pro-business, economic development leader who has spent his career creating a strong economy. He highlights bringing Intel's chip manufacturing facility to Licking County as the largest economic development deal in Ohio state history.

Immigration: Husted supports aggressive border security and immigration enforcement, citing his deciding vote for the One Big Beautiful Bill that provided $170.7 billion for border enforcement. He frames every state as a border state and credits the Trump-Vance administration for progress stopping illegal immigration.

Criminal justice & public safety: Husted identifies as a champion of law enforcement, having secured millions in funding for police agencies. His campaign highlights record-breaking endorsements from 75 Ohio sheriffs and the Fraternal Order of Police, underscoring his commitment to public safety and the rule of law.

Government accountability & ethics: As Lt. Governor, Husted led regulatory reform to implement technology, eliminate fraud and waste, and save taxpayer dollars. He founded InnovateOhio to reduce government costs and implemented digital services like online driver's license renewal to cut in-person government visits.

Economy & cost of living: As Speaker of the Ohio House, Husted led passage of what he calls the most fiscally conservative budget in 40 years and delivered the largest income tax cut in Ohio's history at that time, positioning himself as a fiscal conservative.

Jobs & labor: Husted positions himself as a reliable partner for growing Ohio's economy and creating good-paying jobs, highlighted by bringing Intel to Licking County and pioneering job training through business-driven programs like TechCred and Industry Sector Partnerships.
Other: Husted identifies as a champion for life, framing his pro-life stance through his personal history of starting in foster care before being adopted by his parents, Jim and Judy Husted.

Economy & cost of living: Husted states the campaign's shared commitment is to grow Ohio's economy, strengthen communities for working families, and protect the values Ohioans believe in, framing these as the core priorities of his Senate run.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: The campaign calls for ending gerrymandering, overturning Citizens United, shutting down dark money, reinstating and strengthening the Voting Rights Act, expanding early voting and vote-by-mail, same-day registration, and replacing the Electoral College with direct presidential election.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign proposes creating millions of good-paying jobs by rebuilding America's infrastructure from roads and bridges to docks and jetties, and putting high-speed broadband in every rural community.

Education: The campaign supports reducing class sizes in elementary schools, bringing back shop classes and technical education, and giving every young person who wants to the chance to go to college debt-free.

Jobs & labor: The campaign fights for workers' rights to form unions and negotiate strong wages and benefits, and opposes trade policies that ship jobs overseas, framing these as essential to a nation of opportunity for all.

International affairs: The campaign opposes Trump's war in Iran as illegal and unconstitutional, commits to voting for War Powers Resolutions to end the conflict, and asserts that the power to declare war belongs to Congress, not the President.

Housing: The campaign states that housing and child care should be affordable in every community and to every family, as part of its broader vision of opportunity for all Americans regardless of background.

He supports St. Gabriel's Call and Rhode Island Right to Life, which help mothers with diapers, baby clothes, free ultrasounds, and ongoing support, and calls for empathy toward women after abortion.

Immigration: Bahry opposes mass deportations of good hardworking people while the legal immigration system remains broken. On gender, he opposes medical transitioning for young people, saying children deserve honesty, counseling, compassion, and time rather than irreversible procedures.

Economy & cost of living: Bahry argues ending wars would free trillions for infrastructure, innovation, and education, driving growth and reducing poverty. He states war and military spending are not sustainable job programs, and that peace enables nations to collaborate on climate solutions and sustainable development.

Other: Bahry emphasizes Rhode Island's founding on religious liberty and believes different faiths should be discussed honestly and respectfully, including by politicians. He argues open discussion about faith issues should contribute to how policy is formed and how budgets are formulated, aiming for a more merciful and just society.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Hagerty advocates for the Ratepayer Protection Act, a bill aimed at protecting consumers from rising energy costs. The site presents this as a key advocacy priority of his Senate office.

Government accountability & ethics: Hagerty formally called for the disbarment of former Biden DOJ prosecutor Jack Smith, alleging Smith withheld critical information from a federal court in violation of Tennessee ethics rules.

Other: Hagerty co-filed an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act to improve the permitting process for key technologies that impact national security, streamlining approval for critical tech infrastructure.

antisemitism_education_policy_evidence.summary: Named as a backer of Rick Scott’s June 2023 resolution embracing IHRA; the announcement calls delegitimization of Israel antisemitism. This is resolution sponsorship, not a recorded passage vote.
antisemitism_education_policy_evidence.context: Report date; action may be earlier.

gaza_evidence: 2025-08-01: Hagerty frames Gaza crisis as Hamas propaganda/black-market operation, calls for Hamas surrender, supports GHF over UN/UNRWA as aid mechanism.
2023-10-31: Hagerty questioned Sec. Blinken in a hearing about Gaza funding being diverted by Hamas, pressing on U.S. aid accountability.
2026: AJC voter guide documents Hagerty's strongly pro-Israel record: voted against blocking arms sales to Israel (Apr 15, 2026), supports continued U.S. security assistance, condemns Hamas.
2023-12-15: Hagerty co-introduced UNRWA Reform Act to withhold U.S. funds from UNRWA absent certification of no ties to terrorism or anti-Israel extremism.
2023-02-16: Hagerty pressed State Dept in oversight hearing to confirm Israel must give affirmative consent before any U.S. diplomatic facility (incl. Palestinian consulate) opens in Jerusalem.
2026-07-24: Hagerty on Fox & Friends praises Trump's Abraham Accords expansion and Iran isolation, frames regional security around U.S.-Israel alliance and economic integration.

2026-10: AIPAC PAC endorsed Hagerty for 2026, citing his support for U.S.-Israel relationship and his votes against three resolutions that would have blocked weapons sales to Israel during the war with Hamas.
2022-08: Peace Action tracks Hagerty's voting record on peace issues; his latest tracked action was 2022-08-31, with a lifetime vote score indicating alignment (or lack thereof) with their positions.
2025-09-23: Hagerty posted on X opposing Palestinian state recognition, calling it emboldening Hamas, and praising Trump for refusing to recognize it.
2023-10-31: Hagerty stated on Fox Business that any ceasefire in Gaza is a win for Hamas, opposing ceasefire negotiations.
2021-06-08: Hagerty co-signed letter with Rubio urging Biden not to reopen PLO mission or Jerusalem consulate, opposing 'rewards and incentives to the Palestinian leadership or Hamas.'
2022-06-09: Hagerty issued a statement opposing Biden's plan to create an unofficial US consulate for Palestinians in Jerusalem, framing it as circumventing US law.
2022-06-23: Hagerty and Zeldin led a bicameral joint statement calling on Biden to reverse the plan to create an unofficial US consulate for Palestinians in Jerusalem.
2026-04-15: Hagerty voted Nay on the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 32, blocking a floor vote to disapprove a proposed foreign military sale to Israel (40-59 rejection).

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: Talarico's central campaign theme is fighting billionaire mega-donor influence and political corruption, pledging to bring his anti-corruption fight from the Texas Legislature to Washington to restore power to working people.

Economy & cost of living: Talarico pledges to lower costs for working families by taking on data centers driving up utility bills and ending wars that raise gas prices, working across party lines in the Senate.
Healthcare: Talarico highlights his record of capping insulin costs as a state representative and positions himself as a defender of healthcare access against politicians who gut it.

Education: Talarico emphasizes his record of funding neighborhood schools and expanding opportunities for young adults, rooted in his experience as a middle school teacher in a low-income San Antonio community.
Economy & cost of living: Talarico touts passing the largest property tax cut in Texas history and cutting taxes for small businesses as key legislative achievements benefiting working families.
International affairs: Talarico opposes the war in Iran, arguing it has raised gas prices and sent diesel to record highs, making groceries and cars more expensive for working Texans.

Criminal justice & public safety: Talarico highlights the case of a pedophile who received only one day in jail due to connections to a Paxton donor, positioning himself against corruption in the justice system and for proper accountability for sex offenders.
Jobs & labor: Talarico supports overtime pay for Texas workers and expanding job opportunities for young adults, contrasting his record with opponents who blocked overtime pay legislation.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: The campaign pledges to protect SNAP and Social Security benefits, deliver funding for job training programs, and fund a rural recreational complex to boost local economic development in Alabama's 2nd District.

Healthcare: Figures supports expanding Medicaid in Alabama, saving rural hospitals from closing, addressing maternal-health disparities affecting Black mothers and infants, and defending reproductive rights and patient decision-making.

Other: The campaign proposes tax breaks for parents funding children's extracurricular activities, a tax credit for first-time parents, and exempting baby items such as cribs, mattresses, and baby monitors from tariffs.

Economy & cost of living: Figures introduced legislation for a $15 billion tariff relief program targeting small and mid-sized farmers, and has worked to hold the administration accountable for importing foreign beef below market value, undercutting Alabama producers.

Education: The campaign secured funding for Alabama State University and Tuskegee University, supported capping student loan interest rates, and introduced legislation to cover college and trade school costs for children of first responders, teachers, and social workers.

Transportation: Figures delivered nearly $6 million for roads, ports, and water/sewer projects in the 2nd District and secured a $40 million authorization for future public drinking water and sewer system improvements.

Other: The campaign worked to save the Freedom Rides Museum from sale, preserve the Tuskegee Airmen story in military training, introduce a Tuskegee Airmen monument in Washington DC, and protect all historic civil rights monuments from being sold.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Mendoza pledges to crack down on price gouging, modernize the Child Tax Credit, oppose tariffs that raise costs, strengthen consumer protections in rural communities, and protect and strengthen Social Security benefits for seniors on fixed incomes.

Jobs & labor: Mendoza supports workforce training, apprenticeships, and technical education for good-paying jobs in trades and growing industries. She will support small businesses, bring jobs back to communities, and strongly supports the right to unionize.

Healthcare: Mendoza will reverse cuts to AHCCCS and ACA subsidies, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, oppose privatizing Medicare, and expand coverage to include vision, hearing, and dental.

Immigration: Mendoza supports strengthening border security at ports of entry, deporting violent criminals, holding cartels accountable, professional immigration enforcement, legal pathways to citizenship, oversight of detention facilities, and the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act.

Environment & climate: Mendoza will invest in clean energy, protect local solar projects, keep utility costs from rising, strengthen water infrastructure, secure Arizona's Colorado River share, protect groundwater, clean up PFAS contaminants, and push for a five-year Farm Bill.

Government accountability & ethics: Mendoza supports banning members of Congress and top officials from trading individual stocks, strengthening transparency laws, reinstating town halls, launching community events across AZ-06, and adopting a mobile-first constituent engagement platform.

Other: Mendoza will restore VA funding cut by DOGE, expand rural VA specialty care, improve telehealth access, strengthen mental health services, expand housing support, modernize VA electronic health records, and protect veterans from predatory claim sharks.

International affairs: Mendoza supports diplomacy, working with allies, honoring NATO, securing the Southern border, rebuilding the partnership with Mexico, requiring Congressional approval before committing troops to new conflicts, and exhausting diplomatic options before military action.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Adam Gray prioritizes lowering the cost of food, housing, utilities, and healthcare for Central Valley families. He has introduced bills to reverse Medicaid cuts, extend ACA tax credits, limit presidential tariff authority, and reduce regulatory burdens on energy and food production.

Environment & climate: Water access is the top issue in the district. Gray has introduced multiple bills to authorize new water storage projects, ease permitting and environmental review timelines, codify emergency water measures, and secure funding for interties and wastewater treatment in Valley communities.

Other: Gray supports Valley agriculture through Farm Bill passage, protecting the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program, securing economic assistance for specialty crop growers, incentivizing precision agriculture technology, and creating a pathway for undocumented farm workers to earn legal status.

Education: Gray supports quality education from K-12 through college, including funding for school-based mental health programs, building medical schools in underserved areas, full IDEA funding for children with disabilities, agricultural technology training, and Head Start programming.

Criminal justice & public safety: Gray strongly supports law enforcement and opposes policies he links to retail theft rings, including zero bail (Prop 25), reduced sentencing (Prop 47), and early release (Prop 57). campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Dalton's stated first priority is making Florida affordable again by reversing healthcare premium hikes and illegal tariffs, cracking down on power companies and property insurers raising rates, raising the federal minimum wage, and passing the PRO Act to strengthen labor unions.

Healthcare: Restore Medicaid funding, reverse premium cuts, protect Social Security and Medicare, negotiate drug prices like other wealthy countries, build on the ACA to lower premiums and surprise bills, and codify Roe into federal law to protect reproductive autonomy.

Government accountability & ethics: The EXPEL Plan calls for banning congressional stock trading, banning federal employees from betting on prediction markets, overhauling the ethics committee, requiring independent audits of financial disclosures, stripping pensions from ethics offenders, outlawing taxpayer-funded hush money, and banning former members from becoming lobbyists.

Housing: Enable creation of more housing at all income levels to increase supply, and ban Wall Street speculators from buying up single-family homes, which reduces options for families and drives up costs for everyone else in Central Florida.

Economy & cost of living: Provide immediate tax relief for Florida families while tackling wasteful federal spending, including opposing billion-dollar expenditures on executive jets, Pentagon plaques, and foreign bailouts, and addressing the national debt as a national security threat.

Environment & climate: Support an all-of-the-above energy policy to strengthen energy independence and reduce reliance on foreign oil and Chinese solar, while preventing offshore drilling off Florida's coasts and protecting military and space ranges like Eglin Gulf and the Eastern Range.

International affairs: Support robust national security and border security infrastructure, but avoid more forever wars in the Middle East, set clear strategic goals for military operations, and ensure overseas spending generates adequate return on investment rather than funding bloated international bureaucracies.

Criminal justice & public safety: Uphold the Second Amendment as a fundamental right for law-abiding citizens while keeping firearms out of the hands of violent criminals, and ensure police departments are fully funded with the resources they need to keep communities and schools safe.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Casey Askar states that tackling the rising cost of eggs, milk, and gas is his top priority. He pledges to work with leadership to slash overburdening taxes and regulations contributing to the affordability crisis.

Immigration: The campaign calls for continued deportation of criminal illegal aliens, securing all borders and points of entry, and maintaining a merit-based America First immigration policy. It frames eliminating illegal immigration as a bipartisan endeavor.

Healthcare: The campaign pledges to end Obamacare and replace it with a new vehicle for all Americans. It also commits to cracking down on government waste and fraud to preserve Medicaid and Medicare, and lowering drug and insurance costs.

Parental rights in schools: The campaign asserts parents should ultimately decide how to educate their children, opposes what it calls un-American and socialist education reforms, requires civics teaching in schools, and states biological boys do not belong in girls' bathrooms.

Environment & climate: The campaign calls for unleashing U.S. domestic energy production to power the economy and national security, specifically expanding oil, natural gas, nuclear, and clean coal production to reduce reliance on foreign oil.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign identifies banning members of Congress from stock trading as a priority and calls for exposing and eliminating a culture of corruption within the federal government, including in Congress, demanding full transparency.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: The campaign supports mandatory Real ID and immigration status verification as conditions for voting, arguing only American citizens should vote. It also pledges to prevent foreign actors like China and Russia from compromising the election system.

International affairs: The campaign calls for pushing back against Communist Chinese aggression in the Western Hemisphere, continuing to fund and modernize the military under an America First peace-through-strength policy, and working with allies to defend shared values.

Jobs & labor: Proposes imposing a tax on large corporations equal to 100% of government benefits (food stamps, Medicaid) their full-time employees receive, to incentivize living wages. Government accountability & ethics: Advocates for congressional term limits to break the cycle of career politicians, open Congress to fresh perspectives, restore accountability by preventing long-term consolidation of power, and encourage public service as a duty rather than a lifelong career.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Supports a level playing field for American farmers, particularly in Southwest Michigan's diverse agricultural sector including specialty crops like apples, blueberries, cherries, cranberries, and grapes. Environment & climate: Advocates an all-of-the-above energy strategy that increases energy independence and job creation while encouraging alternative and renewable energy sources and promoting conservation for a cleaner environment, without placing America at competitive disadvantage.

Healthcare: Believes Obamacare has failed; supports patients' rights to choose coverage, curbing junk lawsuits, health savings accounts, empowering states and small businesses to reduce costs, and protecting pre-existing condition coverage through guaranteed access and bans on exclusions.

Other: Prioritizes expanding veteran treatment options, supporting the Forever GI Bill, holding VA accountable, smoothing military-to-civilian transitions with expanded training, and addressing mental health and suicide prevention for service members and veterans.

Economy & cost of living: Fights burdensome regulations on small businesses that increase costs and slow growth. As Financial Services Committee member, oversees agencies including SEC, CFPB, and Federal Reserve to protect investors, maintain fair markets, and facilitate capital formation.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Federal farm policy should avoid burdensome obstacles and be written by farmers, for farmers. Immigration: Keep the border secure, restore the rule of law, resume construction of the southern border wall, and alleviate staffing shortages for Customs and Border Patrol. He secured border security funding through H.R. 1 and co-sponsors the Deporting Fraudsters Act.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Implement common-sense safeguards so only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections and protect individual liberties from what he calls left-wing overreach. He co-sponsored the SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship to register and backed the Equal Representation Act.

Economy & cost of living: Rein in out-of-control government spending as the primary way to address inflation. He voted against the Inflation Reduction Act, opposing its $80 billion for new IRS agents and climate spending, arguing it worsens inflation rather than solving it.
Other: Restore American energy independence as a priority to bring down gas prices and reduce reliance on foreign energy sources, framing it as part of a broader economic agenda for working families.

Economy & cost of living: Opposes federal student loan cancellation as an executive power grab that fuels inflation and forces hardworking Americans to pay for the benefit of higher-income borrowers, arguing it does not address workforce development or higher education costs.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Jake will vote to end massive tariffs and the Iran War, which he says are driving up prices of groceries, gas, and fertilizer. He will also fight corporate monopolies and health insurance companies that raise costs and suppress wages.

Government accountability & ethics: Jake supports term limits, a ban on pardons for family and donors, banning members of Congress from selling stocks and becoming lobbyists, and refuses corporate PAC money. He frames these as core anti-corruption commitments.

Economy & cost of living: Jake will support tax cuts for working families and small businesses, explicitly paid for by raising taxes and closing loopholes for big corporations and the super wealthy. He also pledges to cut red tape to build homes and expand childcare.

Environment & climate: Jake supports a moratorium on new data centers in Southern Minnesota until conditions are met: no increase in electric bills, protection of farmland and water, local economic gains, union jobs, no taxpayer giveaways, and a transparent public process with no NDAs.

Healthcare: Jake will protect Social Security, Medicare, and Veterans benefits, undo recent cuts to Medicaid (Medical Assistance) and SNAP, extend tax credits for health insurance, and fight health insurance companies that extract profits at families' expense.
Housing: Jake will cut red tape to allow quick construction of new homes, expand childcare options, and support small businesses as part of his broader cost-of-living agenda.

Jobs & labor: Jake will work to pass a bipartisan farm bill, ensure farmers have the right to repair their own equipment, and invest in ag innovation that creates jobs in Minnesota rather than abroad.

Government accountability & ethics: Jake will support a balanced budget amendment and vote against raising the debt ceiling until the budget is balanced, framing the $40+ trillion national debt as a corruption and accountability issue.

Environment & climate: Keep public lands accessible for sportsmen, hikers, ranchers, and foresters under the multiple-use mandate. Pass the Public Lands in Public Hands Act to prevent large-scale sale or transfer of federal lands. Prioritize federal funds for boat ramps, campgrounds, trails, and restrooms. Uphold the Taylor Grazing Act and pass the Fill the Lake Act for Flathead Lake.

Government accountability & ethics: Implement no-budget-no-pay and no pay during government shutdowns. Require a mandatory balanced budget amendment at the federal level. Ban congressional stock trading so politicians cannot profit from privileged information. Reduce the net worth inflation of members of Congress funded by taxpayer money.

Environment & climate: Overturn the Cottonwood legal decision to end analysis paralysis on forest management projects. Expand the Good Neighbor Authority so Montana can manage federal forests. End the Roadless Rule to restore public recreation access, timber harvest access, and firefighter access to wildfires.

Economy & cost of living: Cut taxes and reduce regulations to make Montana affordable again. Make permanent working families tax breaks including no tax on tips, overtime, and Social Security. Unleash American energy for abundant, affordable power. Reduce government barriers to building homes and businesses in the state.

campaign_platform_points: Healthcare: The campaign pledges to require Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices, cap insulin at $35/month, create a Medicare-like public option, build on the ACA to limit out-of-pocket costs, and protect reproductive healthcare including abortion, contraception, and IVF access.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign commits to stopping what it calls illegal tariffs, expanding clean energy to lower costs, building affordable housing for first-time buyers, keeping healthcare premiums down, and investing in affordable childcare and Head Start programs.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign proposes banning congressional stock trading, a lifetime lobbying ban for members, term limits, a Supreme Court ethics code, overturning Citizens United, limiting presidential pardon power, and addressing government waste.

Immigration: The campaign supports securing borders with personnel and technology while creating a fair path to citizenship for long-term immigrants and Dreamers, legal work visas for essential industries, and demanding accountability for ICE abuses.

Education: The campaign pledges to expand affordable childcare, restore the Child Tax Credit to $3,600 permanently, strengthen community colleges and state universities, and invest in vocational and apprenticeship programs in high schools.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign supports fully funding police with training and mental health support, reauthorizing the Violence Against Women Act, universal background checks, red flag laws, and community violence intervention programs.

International affairs: The campaign calls for reestablishing USAID, rebuilding relationships with key allies, strategic military investment against threats from China and Russia, and demanding congressional oversight of military actions.
Environment & climate: The campaign supports expanding clean energy production to reduce costs for families in the short term while protecting the environment in the long run.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: The campaign pledges to cut red tape, increase housing supply and construction, fully restore the SALT deduction, lower energy costs through clean domestic energy, pass paid family leave, and fully fund elder care to make life more affordable for New Jersey families.

Jobs & labor: The campaign aims to position New Jersey as a national leader in clean energy, biotech, and AI; fund job training and apprenticeships for good-paying jobs without a college degree; implement predictable trade policy; support workers' rights and unions; and modernize infrastructure including the Gateway Tunnel.

Healthcare: The campaign commits to protecting pre-existing condition coverage, restoring Medicaid and Medicare cuts, increasing mental health services especially for youth, opposing NIH cuts, streamlining cross-state licensing for healthcare professionals, and shifting provider incentives toward health outcomes rather than procedure volume.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign supports commonsense gun safety reforms, removing weapons of war from civilian access, supporting law enforcement resources and community trust, addressing the mental health crisis, reimplementing the silencer tax, and restoring CDC gun violence research funding and the White House Office of Gun Violence Prevention.

International affairs: The campaign pledges to prepare for 21st-century warfare including cyber, drone, and AI threats; improve DoD technology acquisition; counter China as the top strategic threat over the next 50 years; maintain an apolitical military; and preserve America's role as a reliable global partner for peace and democracy.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: The campaign supports restoring a woman's right to choose at the federal level, protecting voting rights and making registration easier, advancing the Equality Act for LGBTQ+ rights, and working with bipartisan lawmakers on immigration reform and trade.

Environment & climate: The campaign commits to maintaining environmental regulations, removing forever chemicals and lead from drinking water, preserving environmental grants, investing in climate-resilient infrastructure, supporting family farms against extreme weather, and incentivizing renewable energy, solar, and electric vehicles.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign pledges to pass a ban on Members of Congress trading stocks, pass real campaign finance reform to prevent billionaires from buying elections, and hold the current administration accountable for ignoring judicial orders and constitutional checks on executive power including Congress's spending authority.

Education: Titus has made quality education for all a priority throughout her career, advocating for class size reduction in early grades and full-day kindergarten, and has been a strong advocate for the arts at all levels.

Healthcare: Titus sponsored legislation creating the Nevada Check-Up program to cover uninsured children and a law allowing seniors and other Nevada residents to purchase cheaper prescription drugs from Canada.

Criminal justice & public safety: Titus led efforts against sexual predators with legislation requiring life supervision, creating a public website to identify where registered offenders live, and banning them from living near schools, parks, and other places where children gather.

Housing: The campaign outlines plans for housing as a top priority in the 2026 reelection bid. Titus has a track record of advocating for affordable housing, including the Dina Titus Estates, an innovative affordable housing complex for persons with disabilities.

Government accountability & ethics: Titus is demanding answers about why officials did not consult residents before approving a data center on federal land in Boulder City, and is urging the governor to pause tax abatements tied to similar projects until lawmakers can review them.

Healthcare: Dina Titus co-sponsored and voted to pass the Women's Health Protection Act to codify Roe v. Wade into federal law, and has repeatedly called for the Senate to end the filibuster to pass this legislation, framing it as essential to women's equality.

campaign_platform_points: Healthcare: The campaign's top stated priority is protecting healthcare access, specifically safeguarding Medicare and Medicaid while working to reduce the financial burden of medical costs on families in the district.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign pledges to focus on lowering everyday costs for working families, specifically targeting groceries, housing, prescriptions, and other basic needs. It also proposes exploring a tax on extraordinary oil profits to fund rebates for low- and middle-income households.
