Environment & climate: Supports maintaining and enhancing parks, trails, and recreational areas for all residents, and protecting open spaces to preserve the natural beauty and character of Morgan Hill.

Housing: Supports diverse housing options and strategies that maintain affordability for families, seniors, and workers without compromising neighborhood safety or charm. Any future growth must be responsible, with developers held accountable.

Transportation: Committed to improving traffic flow, expanding safe pedestrian and bike routes, supporting reliable public transit, and advocating at county and state levels for funding and policies to keep Morgan Hill connected.

Economy & cost of living: Supports revitalizing downtown by strengthening local businesses, improving infrastructure, enhancing pedestrian safety, and ensuring access for seniors and all community members to generate healthy revenue for city services.

Economy & cost of living: Supports promoting wineries, outdoor recreation, sports facilities, and local events to benefit residents and small businesses, while protecting the community's small-town feel through smart planning.

Government accountability & ethics: Advocates for a City Council environment characterized by respect, professionalism, and collaboration, where members listen to one another, disagree respectfully, and stay focused on solutions to earn resident trust.

Education: Supports developing programs that connect city staff with the school district to ensure education is accessible, well-supported, and aligned with community needs, providing students with resources and safe environments.

Housing: Maintain strong tenant protections including for mobile home owners so existing residents are not displaced by new development. Adopt single-stair reform so small lots can become mid-rise, family-sized apartments.

Transportation: Build a connected network of protected bike lanes linking neighborhoods, schools, parks, downtown, and transit. Implement Vision Zero by redesigning dangerous streets. campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports thoughtful housing creation for renters, families, seniors, mobile home residents, first-time homebuyers, and workers. Backs strong tenant protections, affordable housing development and preservation, community ownership models, R3 zoning for stacked flats, a local alternative plan for SB79 neighborhoods, and a Mobile Home Rent Stabilization Ordinance.

Homelessness: Advocates for expanding safe parking programs with county financial support, increasing truly affordable housing, and providing protections for seniors and women facing domestic violence. Supports regional efforts to prevent homelessness and help homeless residents long term.

Economy & cost of living: Supports small businesses by expanding business districts, cutting red tape, and making permitting easier and quicker. Champions a Business Investment District for Castro Street to fill vacant storefronts, neighborhood retail centers, and supporting innovative tech companies to create sustainable jobs.

Environment & climate: Pushes for carbon neutrality by 2040, ending natural gas, meeting tree planting goals, preserving open space and biodiversity, eliminating toxic chemicals in landscaping, and incentivizing greener building materials. Supports equitable electrification including balcony solar and public EV charging.

Transportation: Supports expanding free shuttle routes and frequencies for workers, families, students, and seniors. Advocates for safer biking and pedestrian infrastructure including safe routes to school, evaluation of e-bike and e-scooter speed and age regulations, and equitable clean energy solutions.

Other: Supports adopting a city-level AI use policy to ensure appropriate use of AI tools, prevent elimination of jobs, and manage data privacy concerns as AI becomes more prevalent in municipal operations.

Environment & climate: The campaign presents environmental sustainability and climate action as a core priority, citing work to unite leaders to pass climate legislation in Mountain View and other jurisdictions, and ongoing advocacy for sustainability and community education.
Economy & cost of living: The campaign states a commitment to supporting local businesses in Mountain View as part of its broader platform for the city's economic well-being.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports SB 79 transit-oriented housing but will push Mountain View to use the local alternative plan provision to protect historic corridors, mobile home parks, and existing lower-income neighborhoods from displacement-driven demolition.

Housing: Supports completing the R3 zoning update with form-based standards that favor stacked flats, duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes over large townhome developments, arguing this missing-middle infill fits existing neighborhoods and generates more affordable units.

Housing: Will defend and strengthen the Mobile Home Rent Stabilization Ordinance, ensure the SB 79 local alternative plan exempts mobile home parks, and require funded relocation assistance before any infrastructure project displaces inhabited RVs.

Housing: Will push to ensure city affordability programs reach families at 50–80% AMI and below, who are most at risk of displacement and least served by market-rate housing, beyond the current 80–120% AMI target.

Transportation: Fully supports Vision Zero to eliminate traffic fatalities by 2030 through bike lanes, protected intersections, safe routes to school, and traffic calming, requiring anti-displacement plans before any infrastructure project moves forward.

Criminal justice & public safety: Advocates for a fully funded, standing mental health co-responder program (not a pilot) deploying trained civilian mental health workers alongside or instead of police for appropriate calls, treating mental health as a public health issue.

Government accountability & ethics: Will push for community briefings within 60 days of any major state law or policy change, translated materials as the default, and neighborhood-level meetings so participation does not require a car or a half-day off work.

Government accountability & ethics: Will hold the council to Measure G's 20–25% affordable housing allocation, push for annual plain-language translated public reporting on units created and income levels served, and ensure specific projects like Lot 12 on Castro Street are delivered on time and budget.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign supports a package of federal gun safety measures including an assault weapons ban, expanded background checks, safe storage laws (Ethan's Law), bump stock bans, and increased research funding to reduce gun violence in Oakland.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign advocates for evidence-based community violence intervention programs that proactively address the root causes of violence before incidents occur, combining prevention with enforcement, mental health resources, and community investment.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign commits to ensuring transparency in how tax dollars are spent and holding City Hall accountable, citing residents' long-standing frustration with a lack of accountability from city government.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign prioritizes economic growth that specifically supports local businesses, stating that Oakland businesses deserve the support they need to thrive and that strong businesses create jobs and contribute to the city's financial stability.
Housing: The campaign lists housing stability for Oakland families as a core priority in its stated vision for the city, alongside public safety, accountability, and neighborhood services.

campaign_platform_points: Homelessness: The campaign commits to cutting unsheltered homelessness in half over five years, building 1,600 affordable housing units (800 for homeless), connecting people to mental health and addiction services, cleaning up encampments, and providing emergency shelter.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign advocates a comprehensive, community-focused public safety strategy combining gun violence reduction (Operation Ceasefire), prevention programs, police academies, and anti-trafficking efforts, citing homicides at a 58-year low and violent crime down 22%.

Housing: The campaign pledges to expand affordable and accessible housing across Oakland, with 1,600 units in construction or breaking ground in 2026, including units set aside for people leaving homelessness and senior housing.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign is finalizing a Charter Reform vision through a working group co-chaired by League of Women Voters and SPUR, aiming to improve transparency, efficiency, and accountability in City government after gathering input from over 1,150 residents.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign prioritizes reducing red tape for small businesses by fast-tracking permits, expanding same-day digital approvals, and streamlining zoning clearance to attract and retain businesses in commercial corridors like Downtown and Broadway Valdez.

Immigration: The campaign prohibits use of city property for federal immigration enforcement, orders OPD not to act at the direction of the National Guard or federal authorities, and established a citywide task force to protect residents' civil rights.

Environment & climate: The campaign commits to escalating cross-department wildfire operations, maintaining all fire stations open and operational, clearing high-risk brush with goats, and securing state grants to expand fire coverage in East Oakland hills.

Other: The campaign invests in youth programs including expanding the Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program to 1,050 young Oaklanders, reopening the Mosswood Recreation Center, and restoring OPD Cadets as a career pathway for young adults.

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Repeal restrictive police ordinances (police commission, sanctuary limits, pursuit speed cap, excessive force reporting), grow OPD from 714 to 1,000 officers by 2027, terminate federal oversight of OPD, and close the MACRO program in favor of treatment centers.

Criminal justice & public safety: Establish a joint OPD-DEA-CHP drug task force of 50 officers, adopt San Francisco's DMACC model for coordinated enforcement in East Oakland, clear open-air drug markets, and shut down illegal cannabis warehouses masking fentanyl operations.

Economy & cost of living: Oppose new bond measures and additional city debt; restructure existing debt interest payments; provide tax incentives for small and medium businesses and new manufacturing; increase Oakland Port productivity; and redevelop East and West Oakland with federal assistance.

Homelessness: Provide immediate rehabilitation for homeless individuals with drug or mental health issues; house severely disabled individuals in proper facilities; offer jobs, trade schools, and on-the-job training with a U.S. citizenship requirement; and provide accessible housing for working citizens.

Education: Overhaul Oakland's education system by funding specialized classes for struggling students, expanding arts and science curricula, ensuring after-school programs, redirecting $5 million from underperforming NGOs to youth programs, and creating more trade schools for youth.

Jobs & labor: Attract Physical AI, robotics, and advanced manufacturing companies to West Oakland; create apprentice programs training and hiring only Oaklanders; and reduce business permitting to 30 days or less to spur economic growth and job creation.

Government accountability & ethics: Commission a full outside audit of city finances including all nonprofits and NGOs; redirect funds from failed programs like MACRO to police, fire, and small businesses; and stop what the campaign calls a flood of taxpayer money to unaccountable organizations.

Housing: Provide accessible housing for working Oaklanders who cannot afford market-rate housing, with the explicit requirement that recipients must be American citizens. Framed as part of a broader homelessness and economic strategy.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Increase real estate transfer fees to fund social housing and community land trusts; convert vacant buildings and public land into permanently affordable housing; ban corporate land looting and limit speculative investment to stabilize neighborhoods and reduce displacement.

Criminal justice & public safety: Invest in street repairs including pothole filling, light repairs, and deep cleanups; build speed bumps, traffic circles, protected bike lanes, and widened sidewalks; focus enforcement on behaviors causing harm; expand street cleaning and lighting to reduce crime.

Jobs & labor: Fill approximately 1,000 vacant city positions (of roughly 4,000 budgeted but only 3,000 filled) including paving crews, street ambassadors, and crossing guards; reduce barriers to unionized city jobs by expanding hiring pipelines and fighting for competitive compensation.

Homelessness: Expand tiny homes, safe parking, and supportive sites on public land with regular services, sanitation, and pathways to permanent housing and employment; oppose actions that criminalize homelessness; prioritize stability and dignity over encampment sweeps.

Criminal justice & public safety: Expand MACRO (Mobile Assistance Community Responders of Oakland) for non-violent crisis calls; increase proactive outreach to unhoused neighbors; expand fentanyl testing and naloxone access with Alameda County; expand community ambassador programs and the Department of Violence Prevention.

Economy & cost of living: Implement commercial rent stabilization; increase business license fees and payroll taxes on large, highly profitable companies; create a public bank in the East Bay to save on banking fees while investing in affordable housing and local dignified jobs.

Immigration: Ensure sanctuary city policies fully stop ICE from using Oakland departments, funding, and land; end Oakland's use of mass surveillance Flock cameras; oppose city cooperation with ICE deportations and mass surveillance of residents.

Government accountability & ethics: Implement community-led governance with an annual process for residents to set policy priorities; release withheld public records; fully staff community oversight boards to monitor spending transparently; make land use decisions more participatory and responsive to local needs.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Build more homes, streamline permitting to reduce construction delays and costs, protect renters from displacement, expand homeownership pathways, and create permanently affordable housing including community land trusts.

Economy & cost of living: Lower the cost of living for working families through housing production, supporting small businesses, challenging price-gouging corporations, reducing fees that drive up housing costs, and making transportation and childcare more affordable.

Criminal justice & public safety: Pursue a balanced all-of-the-above approach combining first responder resources with violence prevention, mental health response, neighborhood safety programs, well-lit streets, and responsive services to reduce crime and build community trust.

Government accountability & ethics: Demand transparency and results-driven city leadership through clear budgeting, measurable program outcomes, open communication about taxpayer spending, improved oversight, faster responses to neighborhood concerns, and a delivery-focused culture at City Hall.

Homelessness: Bring unhoused residents indoors by keeping shelters open, connecting people to housing and services, focusing on earlier intervention and addiction treatment, converting troubled motels to shelters, and ensuring funding delivers measurable results.

Immigration: Strengthen sanctuary city protections by banning immigration status collection and ICE cooperation, creating ICE-free zones, protecting safety-camera data from immigration enforcement, expanding multilingual services, and connecting undocumented residents with legal aid.

Other: Combat organized sex trafficking through California's first municipal survivor-support fund financed by pimp penalties, a regional anti-trafficking task force, shutting down trafficking-linked businesses, and expanding housing, healthcare, and job support for survivors.

Housing: Allow greater height and density around BART, BRT, major bus corridors, and neighborhood commercial streets, paired with affordable housing, social housing, safer walking and biking infrastructure, and public-realm investments so growth improves surrounding neighborhoods.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports starter and downsizer housing as needed, but opposes being forced to add apartment towers, arguing Orinda has no unmet demand for them. Seeks to use state housing mandates to advance the downtown vision rather than accept high-density projects elsewhere.

Economy & cost of living: Wants to implement the Downtown Precise Plan by finding incentives for landowners to develop feasible projects on downtown sites, growing retail, dining, and entertainment to boost both lifestyle and city revenue.

Criminal justice & public safety: Identifies safety as one of Orinda's defining characteristics, encompassing fire preparedness, traffic and road safety, and maintaining low crime rates as a top priority.

Transportation: Wants to transition the Village side from surface parking lots to a more walkable, lively retail experience, arguing vacant retail sites like Rite Aid and Phair's have higher and better uses than free parking.

Economy & cost of living: Emphasizes careful management of the city's small budget, noting that despite high per capita income, Orinda's sales tax and property tax collections are low relative to its size, and commits to thoughtful spending decisions.

Other: States that preserving Orinda's community character—its village feel, safety for free-range kids, and friendly collegial atmosphere—comes first, even while balancing state-mandated housing and density requirements with local downtown priorities.
Education: Endorses Measure W for high schools, urging voters to support it as a critical need for Orinda's students.

Other: Committed to advancing community projects including a major community park update, converting the Kindergym into a tech-enabled meeting facility, implementing a facade improvement program, and starting high-quality housing projects to fill vacant downtown spaces.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Pacifica has operated under a structural deficit for years. Meiman will work with City staff and the community to bring new revenue sources to the City, taking a pragmatic approach that balances progress with environmental protection.

Homelessness: Pacifica's unhoused population grew 40% over two years (161 to 228). Meiman will seek a multifaceted, regional strategy guided by compassion while recognizing the general public's right to access public spaces.

Environment & climate: Linda Mar Beach is ranked among the most polluted beaches in the US due to San Pedro Creek runoff during winter rains. Meiman will ensure the City becomes an active partner with environmental organizations in finding and implementing a long-term solution.

Housing: Pacifica needs more housing for young families and individuals, but Meiman opposes projects that would create traffic nightmares or be built in ecologically sensitive areas, citing specific concerns about Pedro Point field and San Pedro Mountain.

Housing: Meiman supports the 2025 short-term rental ordinance and will fight to extend it, including the primary residence requirement for STR operators, to Pacifica's coastal zone. The goal is visitor coastal access, transient occupancy tax revenue, and thriving residential communities.

Government accountability & ethics: Meiman will use her teaching experience to make City government more accessible and transparent: investigate issues, educate the public, envision solutions, and implement them together with residents, so government operations no longer feel like a maze.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: As Housing Committee Chair, Lauing led zoning and policy changes to meet state requirements while shaping where growth occurs, including deed-restricted below-market-rate homes beyond state mandates. In a second term he will pursue funding, partnerships, and incentives to build additional truly affordable homes.

Criminal justice & public safety: Lauing supports renewed investment in police and fire staffing, recruitment, training, equipment, and oversight. He acknowledges hiring and retention remain serious challenges and commits to ensuring public safety departments have the people, training, accountability, and resources to serve every part of the community.

Environment & climate: Lauing advocates turning Palo Alto's climate commitments into practical, affordable programs including modernizing the electric grid, supporting electrification, protecting the urban forest and natural areas, and preparing for climate impacts. He emphasizes solutions that are ambitious, equitable, and implementable.

Other: Lauing emphasizes planning new development as complete neighborhoods rather than collections of buildings, preserving what works in existing neighborhoods, ensuring residents are heard in shaping the path forward, and investing wisely in community needs to keep Palo Alto strong, connected, and livable.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Community safety requires more than excellent police and fire departments; it also means investing in safe streets, well-maintained infrastructure, emergency preparedness, and a strong connected community where residents look out for one another.

Government accountability & ethics: Committed to fiscal responsibility, protecting taxpayer dollars, transparent community engagement, and ensuring every voice in Piedmont is heard and valued in local decision-making.

Housing: Supports creating new and affordable housing and responsibly meeting state housing mandates while ensuring Piedmont retains its hometown feel. Advocated for equitable, accessible, and affordable housing throughout her career.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Supports ALPRs as a law enforcement tool but calls for community discussion on updating Piedmont's policy, ensuring residents understand how systems are used and who can access data, and requiring thorough mandatory audits.

Economy & cost of living: Supports Measure GG, which would increase Piedmont's real estate transfer tax by 0.45 percentage points from 1.3% to 1.75%. Would not commit in advance to fund allocation but would consider it within the city's overall budget and long-term financial planning.

Other: Identifies Piedmont's top infrastructure needs as maintaining and improving streets and sidewalks, upgrading stormwater and sewer systems, and maintaining and modernizing public facilities including parks and recreational facilities.

Jobs & labor: Supports fair and competitive pay for all Piedmont employees including police and fire, consistent with what the city can responsibly afford, in response to union requests for health benefits and retention pay.

Environment & climate: Advocates for long-term environmental and financial sustainability while investing in infrastructure and planning for the future, as part of preserving Piedmont's community character.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Gonzalez opposes the AVAIO Perseus Data Center project and all its future phases, which are proposed for the former Delta View Golf Course site in Pittsburg.

Government accountability & ethics: Gonzalez pledges to make city government more effective, efficient, inclusive, and responsive by requiring department leaders to institute customer service standards, acquire training and technical skills, and recruit volunteers and part-time workers to support public servants.

Criminal justice & public safety: Gonzalez proposes funding more prosecutions of crime and vandalism to hold repeat offenders accountable, expanding neighborhood watch programs using public and private video cameras, and changing recent laws he says left minor theft and vandalism without consequences.

Government accountability & ethics: Gonzalez commits to making city budgets, revenue, expenses, and investments easier for residents to access, encouraging broader community participation in how tax dollars are spent, and prioritizing resources for the most vulnerable residents.

Housing: Gonzalez plans to meet with housing developers active in the past eight years to ask what government can do, including changing regulations, to increase affordable housing; if private or public-private solutions fail, he says government must take a more aggressive role.

Criminal justice & public safety: Gonzalez supports building trust between Pittsburg police and residents, providing officers with quality training, modern equipment, body cameras, and resources, while also insisting on accountability and transparency when misconduct occurs.

Homelessness: Gonzalez proposes creating a comprehensive, updated database of the unhoused population, then building cross-agency teams to address each person's unique needs individually, with the goal of helping everyone achieve sustainable warm shelter and food and reintegration into the community.

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Comprehensive public safety strategy combining accountability with upstream prevention: expand mental health crisis response, fund evidence-based violence prevention programs, create youth opportunity pathways, address housing instability, and ensure a well-staffed police department with modern training and ethical standards.

Economy & cost of living: Support small and mid-sized businesses by cutting red tape, improving access to resources, and making city government a partner rather than an obstacle for local entrepreneurs. Also revitalize Downtown Richmond and Hilltop Mall as commercial anchors.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports building 'missing middle' housing (duplexes, triplexes) via streamlined approvals, by-right zoning, ADU conversions, and transit-oriented development. Expands tenant protections including just-cause eviction and rent stabilization. Creates social housing on public land. Supports state Proposition 1 ($11.25B bond) for affordable housing.

Government accountability & ethics: Will build consensus on City Council to end gridlock, push stalled developments (Speedway at Bayfair Phase II, Marina projects) forward, create Opportunity Zones on the west side, and conduct administrative reviews while protecting essential public safety and community programs.

Economy & cost of living: Flags the shift from an $18M surplus to an $11.5M projected shortfall. Demands a top-to-bottom financial review, opposes raising taxes on homeowners and businesses for 'runaway spending at City Hall,' and says the city must get serious about taxes, bonds, and regulations.

Criminal justice & public safety: Supports full-strength police and quality investigations. Will build alternative response units with mental health professionals for behavioral health crises. Supports ALPR for tracking stolen vehicles and warrants but opposes using ALPR to surveil or track residents. Will leverage the Community Police Review Board.

Transportation: Acknowledges San Leandro ranks 'second from the bottom' in Alameda County for road condition. Will hold open public meetings before major road investment decisions, prioritize regional and state grants for repairs, and advocate for transit-oriented development placing residents near public transit.

Jobs & labor: Will aggressively recruit businesses to fill vacant storefronts and strip malls, advocate for high-tech training centers leveraging local universities and labor unions, and has asked Council for a temporary AI Data Center Moratorium to consult the community before approving such developments.

Homelessness: Supports a Housing First approach: moving people into safe temporary housing paired with counseling, job training, and supportive services. Will leverage Alameda County funds and non-profit partners to convert unused spaces into dignified housing, and coordinate with neighboring cities on shared housing opportunities.

Other: Will upgrade and maintain parks, trails, and recreational facilities as community hubs. Supports pedestrian safety, expanded bike networks, and neighborhood beautification. Will bridge the gap between the City and San Leandro Unified School District to share facilities and create low-cost recreation opportunities.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Made quality of life a central council focus, advancing the CalTrans Clean California initiative for neighborhood beautification, supporting investments in parks, libraries, youth programs, and summer camps, and working with residents to address traffic, blight, and illegal dumping.

Environment & climate: Advances waste reduction, climate resilience, and wildfire preparedness. Introduced referrals to reduce single-use food packaging and explore home hardening. Advocates for evaluating environmental impacts of AI data centers on water, energy, and infrastructure before approval.

Economy & cost of living: Makes economic development a top city priority, integrates accessible childcare into the economic development strategy for families and employers, supports public safety and revitalization of commercial corridors to attract investment, and works with regional agencies to bring funding.

Transportation: Advanced the MacArthur Boulevard/Superior Avenue Roundabout for safety, supported Safe Routes to School improvements and neighborhood traffic calming, voted for investments in streets, sidewalks, transportation, and stormwater infrastructure, and advocates for regional transportation funding.

Criminal justice & public safety: Supports investments in police, fire, and emergency preparedness, traffic safety improvements, and blight reduction. Backs balanced public safety strategies combining prevention, enforcement, and community partnerships including the Alternative Response Unit and increased mental health services.

Housing: Supports stronger renter protections and rent stabilization with guardrails for efficacy and accountability. Voted to expand affordable housing and remove barriers to production. Supports homelessness prevention, outreach, and San Leandro's first supportive housing center.

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Opposes Measure H, a quarter-cent sales tax, arguing the city must first control spending, eliminate waste, scrutinize contracts and consultants, and prioritize essential services before asking residents for more money.

Criminal justice & public safety: States that public safety is government's first responsibility, with police, fire, 9-1-1, emergency response, and streets as top-priority essential services that residents should feel safe in every neighborhood.

Housing: Supports smart, balanced housing that teachers, nurses, firefighters, police officers, young families, and working people can afford, while ensuring growth is planned in a measured way considering traffic, parking, infrastructure, schools, and neighborhood quality of life.

Government accountability & ethics: Commits to making City Hall more transparent and accountable, insisting on measurable results for programs, asking tough questions about how tax dollars are spent, and ensuring residents know how decisions are made.

Economy & cost of living: Proposes expanding the city's economic base by retaining existing businesses, filling commercial vacancies, and attracting new employers as an alternative to raising taxes, and recovering vehicle license fee revenue owed by the State.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: Minimize closed-door council meetings so the community is not kept out of governance. Founded Open Governance News (OpGov.News) to educate residents on how decisions are made and hold authorities accountable. Committed to ensuring no local election goes unchallenged.

Environment & climate: Supports and would expand open-space protection under Measure G. Opposes the October 2025 council action that abolished the protection without meaningful discussion, and pledges to preserve and expand open-space safeguards rather than remove them.

Housing: Advocates encouraging construction of starter homes to address declining population and school enrollment. Argues that building townhomes alone to meet RHNA numbers is insufficient and that essential staff need local housing to remain in the community.

Economy & cost of living: Supports a thriving local small-business ecosystem as a source of future entrepreneurship. Pledges to conduct regular workshops addressing small-business challenges and to foster mentoring of youth into business ownership.

Criminal justice & public safety: Believes an engaged, informed community becomes an alert community. Supports regular programs pairing residents with law enforcement and city leadership to structurally build safety into the system rather than relying solely on policing.

Transportation: Calls for long-term traffic planning as essential for any development. Warns that the combined effect of thousands of new townhomes will choke the city and cut off the Windemere and Gale Ranch areas if not addressed proactively.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports meeting state-mandated housing requirements through mixed-use and infill development in the city core to prevent urban sprawl and protect parks/open spaces. Also negotiated inclusionary, affordable workforce housing for teachers, first responders, essential, and healthcare workers.

Environment & climate: Committed to implementing the Climate Action Plan via a Sustainability Advisory Committee, establishing green corridors and firebreaks to reduce carbon footprint and wildfire risk, supporting Smart Growth to prevent sprawl, and investing in renewable energy projects.

Transportation: Prioritizes traffic mitigation (overcrossing, adaptive ramp metering on I-680, fiber-optic smart signals), free teen bus service with no ID required, Youth Ride Free Program, improved Paratransit for seniors and people with disabilities, and safer walk/bike trails.

Economy & cost of living: Aims to strengthen San Ramon's economic profile to attract competitive businesses and tourism through improved community shared spaces and accessible walk/bike trails, while maintaining a AAA financial credit rating and resolving structural deficits.

Education: Negotiated the first free childcare in San Ramon for young working families at no cost to the city, funded by county resources. Also provided high school and college students with internship and political leadership opportunities through Teen Government 101.

Healthcare: Advocates for maintaining and growing the home care provider workforce by providing a living wage, and supports robust, accessible family and senior programs. Draws on personal experience as a parent of a disability survivor to champion disability inclusion.

Jobs & labor: Forges a path toward green jobs and Just Transition, drawing on prior co-chair role of a countywide Labor-Climate Task Force. Supports new well-paying jobs in healthcare, biotech, renewable and alternative energy, and other emerging industries.

Government accountability & ethics: Runs a corporate-free, clean-money campaign and pledges to serve residents without contributions from special interests. Maintained a AAA S&P Global financial credit rating and resolved an inherited $17.6M structural deficit within one year.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports responsible housing development mixing market-rate with low- and very-low-income units integrated into neighborhoods to avoid income segregation. For homelessness, supports expanding transitional and supportive housing, connecting people with services, and working with County partners on mental health, substance-use, and employment barriers.

Criminal justice & public safety: Prioritizes strong, well-staffed Police and Fire Departments with adequate training, equipment, and resources. Emphasizes recruiting and retaining experienced professionals, maintaining response times, and investing in prevention, emergency preparedness, and safe streets alongside traditional law enforcement.

Transportation: Advocates a balanced approach keeping the automobile important while expanding safe walking, bicycling, and public transit alternatives. Supports improving traffic flow, signal coordination, street maintenance, and requiring new development to plan for transportation impacts alongside growth.

Environment & climate: Supports continued investment in clean energy, expanded EV infrastructure, and responsible long-term energy planning through Silicon Valley Power. Also supports protecting local streams and creeks, water conservation, preserving urban tree canopy, reducing waste, and improving energy efficiency of City facilities.

Government accountability & ethics: Demands transparency, responsible spending, and accountability for taxpayer dollars. Prioritizes essential services and infrastructure while questioning unnecessary spending. Also commits to expanding access to affordable and free programs for seniors, children, families, and vulnerable residents.

Other: Pushes for long-term infrastructure planning, preventative maintenance, and responsible investment in streets, parks, public buildings, utilities, and community facilities to avoid costly emergency projects and prevent another massive bond measure on taxpayers.

Other: Believes Levi's Stadium belongs in Santa Clara and will protect the city's interests while building a professional, accountable partnership with the 49ers. Wants stadium events to benefit local businesses and residents while addressing neighborhood impacts like traffic, noise, and quality of life.

Government accountability & ethics: Will work to restore confidence in City Hall through transparency, accountability, respectful leadership, and open communication. Values professional expertise of City employees and commits to working with the entire City Council to find solutions that move the city forward.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Committed to preventing displacement and gentrification in District 5 by supporting truly affordable housing units, a city-wide anti-displacement comprehensive strategy, and preservation policies to protect existing residents and the industrial character of the neighborhood.

Housing: Frames housing as a human right and pledges to secure funding for climate-friendly affordable housing, protect renters from displacement and unfair evictions, increase supply of homes for all income levels, and incentivize mixed-use developments that maximize affordable housing production.

Other: Will fight to bring fully accessible parks to Old Town, revitalize existing playlots, beautify Pecks Lot and Airport Blvd, improve lighting on Linden Avenue corridor, clean up urban blight, and restore historical and cultural spaces through public art and community events.

Healthcare: Seeks to create a new paradigm of connected supportive aging services in District 5, including senior housing, wellness and clinical health support, community spaces, and funding for programs like Project Hope and Meals-on-Wheels to keep older adults connected and healthy.

Healthcare: Advocates for a youth drop-in mental health center, expansion of mental health first aid training, reducing suicide rates, removing mental health stigma, and ensuring mental health crisis calls are staffed by trained clinical providers integrated with public safety teams.

Education: Demands universal access to childcare and after-school care in District 5, securing funding for universal preschool, expanding affordable childcare options, providing information on the city website, and ensuring childcare workers receive a living wage.

Environment & climate: Prioritizes working toward net-zero carbon emissions, investing in renewable clean energy, increasing EV charging access, requiring eco-friendly alternatives to single-use plastics, and incentivizing building electrification while protecting renters from cost pass-throughs.

Economy & cost of living: Committed to empowering small business owners, revitalizing downtown areas with string lighting and walkable streets, attracting new businesses, incentivizing development of abandoned properties, and prioritizing locally owned businesses in District 5 growth planning.

campaign_platform_points: Jobs & labor: The campaign's first stated priority is creating a stronger business environment in Union City to attract more businesses and good-paying jobs, noting the city has been gaining businesses while others lose them.

Other: The campaign calls for increased funding of the Capital Improvement Plan budget to address long-deferred critical infrastructure maintenance, prioritizing building maintenance, faster pothole repairs, and safe, well-maintained parks.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign pledges to fully staff the Police Department to keep neighborhoods safe and crack down on reckless driving, and to keep the Public Works Department fully staffed for roads, parks, and city buildings.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign commits to fiscal responsibility over taxpayer dollars, requiring every new position to be justified by a thorough needs analysis and vowing not to return to the reckless spending that caused the city's prior financial crisis.

Immigration: The campaign states that while regulatory changes like H-2A visa revisions help, administrative actions alone are insufficient and comprehensive immigration reform is still necessary. He has submitted policy proposals to Congress and federal agencies through NLC and NALEO.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Supports rent control protections against displacement, affordable housing construction, strengthened tenant rights, and developer incentives for including affordable units in new developments.

Economy & cost of living: Supports local farmers' markets, food cooperatives, and affordable grocery partnerships to reduce the cost of living, and aims to address food deserts in underserved areas of District 2.
Criminal justice & public safety: Expands mental health and addiction services, invests in community-based safety, improves emergency response times, and funds youth violence prevention programs.

Immigration: Protects immigrant families from discrimination, ensures undocumented residents can access city services, partners with Centro de Servicios, and advocates for every resident regardless of immigration status.

Government accountability & ethics: Calls for transparent budget processes, elimination of inefficient spending, regular taxpayer audits, and direct investment in working family programs at the city level.
Education: Advocates for fully-funded public schools, after-school programs, safe routes to school, and expanded scholarship access for students in District 2.
Transportation: Aims to improve road conditions, expand public transit for working families, invest in pedestrian and bicycle safety, and support development in BART-area zones.
Other: Commits to regular town halls, language accessibility at city meetings, pathways for immigrant civic participation, and an open-door policy for all constituents.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: The campaign prioritizes keeping the Housing Element certified to prevent Builder's Remedy projects, while expanding solutions like ADUs, SB 9, duplex/triplex, and affordable multifamily projects to meet RHNA quotas while protecting the town's semi-rural character.

Housing: Waschura favors working directly with nonprofit affordable-housing developers who use state tax credits and county housing funds, rather than for-profit Density Bonus projects that bundle affordable units with hundreds of market-rate homes.

Criminal justice & public safety: Public safety is listed as a top 2026 priority, encompassing police, fire, and emergency services, safe evacuation routes, wildfire prevention, and efficient capable Town administration.

Environment & climate: The campaign identifies the town's semi-rural character as defined by large lot sizes, deep setbacks, open spaces, pathways, creeks, horse-riding facilities, and landscape screening around development, and commits to preserving these features.

Housing: Higher-density housing should be concentrated near transportation corridors, close to shopping and transit, and where water and infrastructure already exist, rather than scattered up in the hills where roads are narrow and evacuation is at risk.

Other: Waschura argues against codifying Green Sheets founding principles via a ballot initiative, saying it would be under-protective against state mandates and over-restrictive for future governance, and favors carefully drafted ordinances and objective development standards instead.

Housing: The campaign opposes sprinkling small 20-unit-per-acre developments on single-family lots throughout town, arguing they lack economy of scale, lead to concession requests for smaller setbacks and taller buildings, and push infrastructure into the hills.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign emphasizes that good local government depends on transparency, responsiveness, and follow-through, and that Town government should protect community character while planning responsibly for the future.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Increase local control over development decisions while building more affordable housing for working families, seniors, educators, and first responders. Protect renters, ensure new developments match the character of Los Gatos (no towers next to single-family homes), and help older adults age in place.

Criminal justice & public safety: Support and fund police and fire departments for community safety and rapid response. Invest in wildfire prevention, fuel reduction, evacuation planning, and early warning systems. Continue the town's community policing model to reduce crime and build trust.

Transportation: Tackle summer beach traffic by piloting tolling and completing the Highway 17 Congestion Management Project. Build safer, more walkable and bikeable streets, calm neighborhood traffic with smarter roadway design, grow public transit, and pilot free bus passes for students and seniors.

Economy & cost of living: Keep investing in a vibrant downtown, reduce commercial vacancies, stabilize rents, and prioritize local independent shops. Cut red tape that drives up costs for small business owners and continue promoting businesses through events and social media.

Environment & climate: Preserve and enhance open space with wildlife and trail crossings. Enhance parks, add playgrounds and recreation space. Reduce vehicle miles traveled, support climate-smart building to fight climate change, steward trees and creeks, and curb hillside overdevelopment.
Homelessness: End homelessness in Los Gatos through increased behavioral health care and individualized case management, framed as part of the broader public safety and emergency preparedness agenda.

Government accountability & ethics: Maintain fiscal responsibility by strengthening the town's financial transparency and fiscal health without raising taxes. Keep residents informed through newsletters, coffees, social media, and events, and stay open to new ideas and responsive to feedback.

Other: Mentor the next generation of leaders through the Young Leaders Group, expand programs for older adults, champion an intergenerational community center, strengthen family-friendly amenities, and create more third spaces where residents can gather outside of work and home.

comments: Rob is the youngest Mayor and a great supporter of diverse communities.

campaign_platform_points: Housing: Bill Carman will work to meet the state's mandate of 1,118 new housing units over five years while using the Quimby Act to secure new parks and trail access. He describes himself as not pro-development but pro-community, aiming to make forced growth livable while preserving Moraga's semi-rural character.

Environment & climate: Carman commits to protecting Moraga's parks, trails, and open space, and to working to acquire more park land to relieve pressure on school fields and busy multi-use parks. He personally walked and GIS-mapped all Moraga trails in 2018 and states he loves Rancho Laguna exactly as it is.

Criminal justice & public safety: Carman prioritizes disaster preparedness and evacuation readiness, supporting local police, fire, and CERT volunteers. He calls for Zone Zero and Firewise participation, earthquake and flood/mudslide readiness, multiple working evacuation routes, and a shelter-in-place plan, citing insurance pullback from fire-risk areas.

Economy & cost of living: Carman highlights that Moraga receives the lowest percentage of property tax revenue in Contra Costa County, contributing to a $55 million deferred-maintenance backlog. He pledges to support using Measure K funds in the infrastructure manner in which they were originally intended.

Other: Anticipating up to 1,118 new residents who may lack garages or storage, Carman proposes exploring a community tool lending library and maker space as shared resources for a growing town, inviting resident input on the idea.

campaign_platform_points: Criminal justice & public safety: Druker commits to creating and practicing a comprehensive wildfire readiness and evacuation plan across all of Woodside, and establishing neighborhood-level emergency communication groups (cell phone, email, WhatsApp) for rapid alerting during wildfire events.

Housing: Druker supports making it faster and cheaper for property owners to build barns and ADUs, working with local employers to build workforce housing, and planning ahead for RHNA Cycle 7 by addressing the septic-to-sewer infrastructure bottleneck.

Other: Druker commits to preserving Woodside's rural and equestrian character and working with the equestrian community on a strategy to increase the number of horses living and riding throughout the town.

Government accountability & ethics: Druker identifies long-term financial planning as his top priority to ensure Woodside can sustain public safety services over coming decades, and calls for a more responsive, easier-to-work-with local government for residents and businesses.

Other: Druker envisions evolving Woodside town center with more consumer-focused retail, outdoor dining, public gathering spaces, and safe multi-modal access for people, dogs, bikes, and horses, plus completing the roadside trails network.

Education: Druker prioritizes student safety around Woodside Elementary, including the 15 MPH speed limit, crosswalks, traffic calming, parking improvements, and creating safe routes to school for all Woodside children.

Criminal justice & public safety: Druker advocates a coordinated multi-agency 'three E's' approach (Enforcement, Engineering, Education) with CHP, Sheriff, Caltrans, and local officials to stop racing on Skyline Boulevard and protect cyclists and pedestrians at Four Corners.

state.office: At large — full term Governing Board Member / School Director
campaign_platform_points: Education: Accessibility must be built into how schools are planned, maintained, and operated from the start, not added after a student or parent encounters a barrier. The district should know where its barriers are, have a plan, and make that information available to the community.

Education: IEPs and 504 plans are legal rights, not optional favors. The district must deliver the services written into each child's plan without families having to fight or hire lawyers. A clear, direct path must exist to fix missing services immediately, and recurring issues across campuses require district-wide fixes.

Education: Supports a moratorium on generative AI in student work and staff lesson planning, and an end to routine personal-screen use in classroom instruction. Before lifting the pause, AUSD must publicly demonstrate educational benefit, explain privacy protections, and establish safeguards. Learning accommodations and assistive technology remain protected.

Education: During instructional time, phones should be off and away to reduce classroom distractions. However, students should retain reasonable access to their phones for emergencies, and exceptions must be preserved for students whose IEPs, 504 Plans, or medical needs require a personal device.

Education: Schools must be unequivocal that discrimination, harassment, bullying, and targeted slurs based on sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression are not acceptable. Students need clear reporting mechanisms, staff need consistent training, and the Board should verify policies work in students' daily lives.

Education: Will not vote to close neighborhood schools to fix a budget shortfall. Before considering closures, the district should examine administrative costs, consultants, contracts, and vacant positions to identify savings that protect classrooms. Parents and caregivers deserve a clear, simple way to voice views before decisions are made.

Education: Arts education (music, visual art, theatre, dance, media arts) should be part of an equitable education and not depend on which AUSD school a student attends. Will examine school-by-school access, whether students with disabilities can fully participate, and how Proposition 28 funding is used.

Government accountability & ethics: The Board should provide independent oversight, ask hard questions, and follow the evidence rather than rubber-stamping district recommendations. Before cutting classrooms, examine central-office spending, consultants, vacant positions, and contracts without measurable results. Public dollars should be spent transparently with students at the center.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Reading, writing, math, science, and critical thinking must remain central to every student's education. The candidate commits to keeping academic growth and strong classroom learning at the center of all Board decisions.

Education: The candidate will support age-appropriate digital citizenship, media literacy, and healthy technology habits so students can navigate technology, social media, and AI safely and responsibly, while not losing sight of core academics.
Education: The candidate will strengthen two-way communication between the district and families and explore partnerships to expand access to after-school care and preschool for working families.

Government accountability & ethics: The candidate commits to a collaborative governance style: listening to families, educators, staff, and community partners before deciding, communicating openly, and following through from initial conversation through implementation.

Education: The candidate will protect existing strengths in Brisbane's schools—dedicated teachers, engaged families, and community involvement—while pursuing thoughtful, incremental improvements that help every student thrive.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Advocates for competitive teacher compensation to attract and retain educators in high-cost Silicon Valley, while also investing in professional development, mentoring, teacher leadership opportunities, and positive school culture to keep talented teachers in the classroom.

Education: Supports long-term financial planning, transparent budgets, and data-driven decisions about enrollment, staffing, and facilities. Any future school consolidation must be based on reliable data, transparent criteria, meaningful community input, and careful assessment of educational impact.

Education: Prioritizes reasonable class sizes to support effective teaching, protects well-rounded programs including arts, music, science, technology, physical education, and enrichment, and uses multiple measures of student achievement rather than test scores alone.

Government accountability & ethics: Calls for transparent and responsible budgeting, accountability for local funding to ensure resources benefit students, data-informed evaluation of programs, meaningful community input on local priorities, and clear communication about difficult financial trade-offs.

Education: Supports safe and welcoming schools with effective emergency preparedness, strong student mental health and social-emotional learning systems, thoughtful and purposeful use of technology that enhances rather than replaces instruction, and meaningful two-way parent engagement.

Education: Advocates for inclusive and welcoming schools where every student and family is treated with dignity and respect, supports efforts to prevent discrimination and bullying, and believes every child deserves to feel they belong in their school community.

Jobs & labor: Committed to ensuring classified employees—instructional aides, office staff, custodians, maintenance professionals, and other essential team members—have their voices and needs represented alongside certificated staff in district decision-making.

Education: Committed to supporting the whole child through strong counseling programs, wellness centers, social-emotional learning, and other supports that help students feel safe, connected, and ready to learn, linking academic success to student wellness.

campaign_platform_points: Education: The campaign's central pledge is to make academic achievement the district's top priority, arguing CVUSD's performance has declined from excellent to merely average and demanding a leadership change to restore rigor and measurable student growth.

Education: Foster calls for eliminating the district's Equity Grading system (renamed Proportional or Standards-Based Grading), which he argues wastes hundreds of thousands of dollars, lets students earn credit for doing nothing, and produced no meaningful improvement in F-grade rates.

Education: The campaign demands expanding the number and availability of Advanced Placement courses at CVHS, which currently offers fewer than half of available AP courses, and argues the district should survey families to determine true demand and remove seat caps.

Immigration: Harris will ban ICE from community college campuses, advocate for free immigration legal help on campuses, and protect students' personal records and information from immigration enforcement.

Education: Opposes replacing instructors, faculty, or other campus workers with artificial intelligence. Calls for guardrails against AI in every level of government to protect students and workers.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Sasai will advocate for expanding Early and Free College programs and university-transfer pathways at Contra Costa Community Colleges, and deepen partnerships with local unions to expand skilled job training and re-training in an era of AI-driven job displacement.

Education: Sasai commits to fighting federal funding cuts that could result from the dismantling of the U.S. Department of Education, specifically protecting core programs that train firefighters, paramedics, nursing, and healthcare professionals at Contra Costa Colleges.

Government accountability & ethics: Sasai pledges to be a strong steward of taxpayer dollars, ensuring funds go into the classroom rather than bureaucracy, and to provide transparency and accountability on district budget spending to the community.

Education: Sasai will prioritize the continued recruitment and retention of experienced faculty and educational staff at the community colleges, recognizing that more students and families rely on local colleges to save tens of thousands of dollars.

Education: Sasai frames protecting affordability, equity, and diversity in community colleges as urgent in the face of federal attacks on public education, positioning these as core values of his trusteeship.

Jobs & labor: Sasai will deepen partnerships between Contra Costa Colleges and local unions to expand skilled job training and re-training programs, responding to an era where AI is eliminating jobs and replacing workers.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Cooper's top priority is raising academic proficiency in FMSD, where only 28% of students are proficient in math and 35% in ELA. He advocates for more direct instruction, less screen time, homework centers, peer tutoring, and academic competition to prepare K-8 students for high school.

Government accountability & ethics: Cooper prioritizes transparency between the district, schools, teachers, and families. He criticizes the board for not publishing book lists, not notifying parents about classroom activities, and for censuring him for communicating with the community about test scores.

Parental rights in schools: Cooper supports parents' right to choose any school type (regular, charter, private, or homeschool) for their children and to direct their children's education, including the right to opt out of curriculum they disagree with.

Education: Cooper opposes district spending on electronic devices (Chromebooks, iPads, MacBooks, Nintendo Switches) that he argues do not improve student education, advocating instead for more direct instruction and less in-front-of-screen time for students.

Parental rights in schools: Cooper asserts parents must be informed when school staff discuss gender identity or transition with their children, opposing board resolutions that would prevent such notification. He voted against resolutions he characterized as teaching boys to be girls.

Education: Cooper states student safety is paramount and the district's first priority, requiring diligence in ensuring no physical or emotional harm occurs whether children are walking to school, at recess, in classrooms, or in restrooms.

Parental rights in schools: Cooper supports parents' right to opt their children out of curriculum that does not focus on core academics, including social-emotional learning programs he views as placing the school at the center of a child's values development.

Education: Cooper advocates for keeping boys out of girls' sports, locker rooms, and bathrooms, as stated in his official ballot statement as part of his commitment to safe schools with equality for all.

campaign_platform_points: Education: The campaign pledges to maintain and expand four semesters of free tuition for every Gavilan College student regardless of financial need, as part of a broader commitment to removing barriers to college completion.

Education: The candidate commits to setting policy that keeps community college accessible, provides quality programs and guidance, and removes barriers that hinder students from completing their education or career objectives.
Housing: The campaign states it has advanced a student housing plan at Gavilan College and is actively pursuing both state and private funding to make the approved plan a reality.

Jobs & labor: The candidate highlights achieving two consecutive two-year collective bargaining agreements with faculty, initiating the process for student workers to unionize, and raising wages for faculty, staff, and students while maintaining a strong financial reserve.

Education: The campaign credits itself with expanding dual enrollment opportunities that allow high school students to take college courses at their local campuses, improving academic pathways and course offerings.

Criminal justice & public safety: The candidate states he has championed stronger campus security at Gavilan College, along with upgraded technology and data infrastructure and long-overdue repairs to roads, buildings, sidewalks, and HVAC systems.

Government accountability & ethics: The candidate commits to fiscal accountability as a steward of public funds, ensuring taxpayer money directly supports classrooms and programs yield positive student outcomes, while advocating for resource equity so Gavilan receives its fair share.

Education: The campaign states it expanded access to food, transportation, counseling, and health services for students, and committed to partnering with large-scale companies and organizations to create student opportunities and strengthen enrollment and graduation rates.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Develop a new district strategic plan focused on student learning and measurable outcomes to ensure top-tier classroom instruction across the Mountain View Whisman School District.

Education: Adopt a new math curriculum designed to better prepare students for success in high school, college, and careers, replacing the current curriculum with one that improves mathematical readiness.

Education: Strengthen after-school enrichment and academic programs by better aligning them with what students learn in the classroom, so out-of-school activities reinforce and extend classroom instruction.

Education: Offer competitive compensation packages to attract and retain the highest-quality teachers and staff, and support teachers through deeper collaboration and professional development focused on academic standards and instructional practices.

Housing: Continue supporting workforce housing and affordable preschool to help teachers and staff live and work in the Mountain View community, addressing the housing barrier that affects educator recruitment and retention.

Environment & climate: Build stronger community partnerships to make school campuses more climate-resilient and accessible for students and neighbors, integrating climate adaptation into district planning and facility decisions.

Education: Prioritize classroom teaching and learning in the district budget, ensuring that the largest share of public education funds goes directly to instruction rather than administrative or non-instructional spending.

Education: Budget strategically during economic uncertainty to ensure spending aligns with available revenues, and evaluate policies and programs to make every dollar count for students, especially the most vulnerable.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Thida Cornes commits to expanding college and career access, building more pathways for students to discover passions, and setting a clear, sensible AI policy that protects critical thinking and student learning in MVLA schools.

Education: Cornes pledges to develop a system helping more students find a caring adult on campus and a place where they belong, set measurable metrics for belonging, and expand peer-to-peer counseling so students have support from other students.

Government accountability & ethics: Cornes commits to making Board work easier for the community to understand, including translating materials into other languages, and to maintaining an open, accessible, and fiscally responsible Board that is careful with every tax dollar.

Education: Cornes highlights ending the busing of English Language Learners between the two high schools as a key accomplishment, which led to increased English proficiency rates and ELLs scoring green on state standards.

Education: Cornes supports keeping the social studies curriculum accurate and inclusive, training staff to better support LGBTQ+ students, and keeping Health class in person so students receive LGBTQ+ inclusive, medically accurate sex education.

Education: Cornes has grown dual enrollment (college credit classes) and AP access, expanded Career Technical Education pathways including Engineering, Robotics, IT, Digital Communications, Journalism, Culinary, Health Science, and Medical Technology.

Transportation: Cornes commits to continuing collaboration with the City of Mountain View to improve walking, biking, and transportation safety, leveraging her role on the Active Transportation Public Advisory Committee.

Education: Cornes supports the Superintendent Student Advisory Council to give students a direct voice with district leadership, and built a stronger Superintendent performance review process where every Trustee participates equally.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

state.office: District 2 Governing Board Member / School Director
campaign_platform_points: Education: Stabilize OUSD's finances through structural decisions rather than short-term fixes, applying rigorous analysis and making tough necessary decisions while staying grounded in equity.
Education: Develop a comprehensive plan defining what great schools look like in Oakland, how to get there, and how every neighborhood benefits from the district's future.
Education: Center every board decision on whether it improves student outcomes, using evidence-based policymaking to close opportunity gaps and ensure Oakland students graduate ready to succeed.

Government accountability & ethics: Make the school board more open and responsive by ensuring a transparent, community-involved national search process for selecting a new superintendent, rather than opaque decisions without public explanation.

Education: Invest in student mental health, community well-being, and physical school environments that make students want to attend, and use transportation planning expertise to make walking and biking to school safer.
Education: Strengthen college and career pathways, workforce development partnerships, and collaboration with community colleges so every Oakland graduate has a wide range of options after K-12.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

criteria.F: Shields Israel and a strong defender of Israel or has endorsements from Hindutva or Zionist organizations (other than JStreetPAC)
