criteria: Shields Israel and a strong defender of Israel or has endorsements from Hindutva or Zionist organizations (other than JStreetPAC; Zionist organizations explicitly include California Jewish Democrats, the renamed Democrats for Israel California, and its 'Strong Support' tier counts double against the candidate)

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace

state.office: At large — full term Governing Board Member
campaign_platform_points: Education: Wahl supports the San Carlos School District's Measure K, a $489-per-parcel annual tax for 8 years starting July 2027, to fund local education. He emphasizes sustained community investment with clear accountability for maintaining educational quality.

Education: Wahl advocates for stable, responsible funding with transparent oversight to ensure every TK–8 student, including English learners and families navigating new cultural expectations, receives adequate support and opportunity to thrive.

Education: Wahl prioritizes recruiting, supporting, and retaining outstanding educators and staff by strengthening professional continuity and exploring practical housing partnerships and affordability strategies to make sustainable careers in San Carlos possible.

Education: Wahl supports exploring transparent AI uses in schools to reduce administrative burdens and remove barriers to student progress, while protecting privacy, equity, educator judgment, and human accountability. AI should assist, not replace, educators.

Housing: Wahl argues high Peninsula housing costs make it difficult for teachers and staff to live near the families they serve, and the district should explore practical housing assistance, regional partnerships, and affordability strategies.

Government accountability & ethics: Wahl insists on responsible oversight of school spending, including locally controlled revenue, voter-approved uses, independent citizen oversight, annual audits, and public reporting. No funds may be taken by the state or pay administrator salaries.

state.office: At large — full term Governing Board Member
campaign_platform_points: Education: Strengthen student support, belonging, and family partnerships so every child feels safe and supported. Increase awareness of mental-health and counseling resources, identify needs early, foster belonging with a focus on bullying prevention, and support smoother transitions especially into middle school.

Education: Protect strong fundamentals in literacy, math, science, arts, music, and enrichment. Support high-quality instruction and ongoing teacher professional development. Provide appropriate differentiation so students needing extra help receive it while those ready for greater challenge continue to grow.

Education: Treat retaining great educators and staff as a priority. Give educators a meaningful voice in evaluating classroom technology, protect teachers' planning time, reduce unnecessary administrative burden, and ensure staff have input in decisions affecting their work.

Education: In K–8, build strong foundations in reading, writing, math, science, creativity, and critical thinking before introducing technology. Do not make generative AI a routine classroom learning tool for young students. Use technology only where it adds clear value such as accessibility or special-needs support.

Education: Supports Measure K, a $489-per-parcel annual parcel tax for up to eight years, to renew and update local school funding for teachers, small classes, and programs. Emphasizes responsible stewardship, transparency, and an independent oversight committee to ensure funds are used as voters approve.

Government accountability & ethics: Commit to responsible financial stewardship: set clear goals, understand what is being invested, look at evidence of progress, and make the connection between spending and results easy for the community to understand. Ask disciplined questions about what the district is trying to accomplish and how it will be measured.

Housing: Partner with the City of San Carlos to explore creative workforce housing solutions that help school employees afford to remain in the community, addressing the challenge of retaining educators and staff in a high-cost area.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Protect student privacy and carefully evaluate the safety and educational value of new tools before introducing them into schools. Technology decisions should preserve teacher judgment and keep learning at the center, with educators having a meaningful voice in adoption.

campaign_platform_points: Education: The campaign pledges to defend the voter-approved Free City policy that provides free tuition at City College, framing it as a hard-won democratic decision that must be shielded from political attacks.

Education: Every City College board decision should prioritize education, educators, and students above other considerations such as taxes, land use, or transfers, and the candidate will advocate for this from Sacramento to City Hall.

Education: Students should be treated as active voices in shaping their educational future, receiving a holistic education, and the board should actively support student organizing and leadership development.

Education: City College should build positive, reciprocal relationships with the school district and all city departments so that government officials, workers, and residents feel personally invested in the college's future.

Government accountability & ethics: The budget process should begin well in advance with deep planning alongside impacted communities, and must involve transparency and trust-building to reduce future conflict and ensure decisions reflect community voices.
Education: The candidate commits to prioritizing board decisions that increase enrollment at City College, viewing enrollment growth as essential to rebuilding the institution for the city.

Government accountability & ethics: The candidate pledges transparent and fair board decision-making, explaining decisions in clear communication to the extent possible, and committing to long-term accountability rather than treating the board seat as a stepping stone.

Education: The candidate supports expanding dual enrollment so San Francisco Unified School District students can take community college classes while in high school, giving them more resources and a head start on college.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Expand access to advanced coursework and CTE pathways, explore a pathway-style graduation requirement so students go deeper in one field, address the recent dip in A-G completion, and turn assessment data into fast, targeted instruction and intervention.

Education: Ensure the districtwide bell-to-bell phone-free policy is implemented well this fall and that the promised digital citizenship and wellness curriculum is delivered, teaching students healthy tech habits rather than just enforcing a rule.

Education: Move the district's AI policy from task-force recommendations into established classroom practice, including teacher training and clear communication with families about responsible AI use in schools.

Education: Build a district culture of robust, respectful discourse and free expression so students feel comfortable sharing opinions on controversial topics, citing survey data showing only 32% feel comfortable expressing views in class.

Education: Supports the Board's unanimous vote to strengthen nondiscrimination protections for transgender and gender-nonconforming students, including respect for gender identity, use of names and pronouns, equal access to facilities, and dress code freedom.

Education: Lead the district's next Five-Year Strategic Plan, asking hard questions and prioritizing resources around what serves students, while maintaining a balanced, community-funded budget with reserves above the state minimum.

Education: Support careful, well-resourced expansion of the Empower San Mateo wraparound support program (tutoring, mentoring, food pantry) to more school sites as funding and partnerships mature, rather than growing faster than the program can be supported well.

Education: Restore honors and Advanced Standing courses for freshmen and sophomores that were eliminated districtwide, arguing the board should not equalize access by cutting challenging options and should learn from San Francisco's decade-long mistake.

Education: Direct a greater share of the district's $266 million budget toward classroom instruction, noting only 51 cents per dollar currently reaches the classroom while non-instruction spending grew 47% since 2020-21 versus 28% for instruction.

Housing: Use the state's 2022 Teacher Housing Act to build workforce housing on district-owned land and partner with county below-market loan programs to help teachers afford homes in the community, without requiring a new tax or rezoning.

Education: Build real partnerships with local hospitals, labs, colleges, and businesses for internships, mentors, and projects; expand free dual enrollment so students graduate with college credit; and use existing Golden State Pathways funding rather than new taxes.

Education: Provide full English-learner programs at every school that needs one, rather than stretching a couple of aides across a whole school. Area E has more than one in three students still learning English, 1.7 times the rest of the district.

campaign_platform_points: Government accountability & ethics: The district must communicate clearly with the community before and after major decisions. Parents should understand what the district is doing, why, and how their voices fit into the process. Better communication builds trust, which makes better decisions possible.

Education: Before major decisions affecting a school, the board member should visit that school, talk directly with families and staff, and bring community input into the process early rather than after decisions are made.

Education: The board should establish clear, open processes for major appointments (such as principals) and policy decisions, ask hard questions, expect clear answers, and do the work before casting a vote.
Education: Budgets should be made easier to understand for taxpayers. The board must clearly explain what is being spent and why, and show the connection between dollars spent and student outcomes.

Education: Students do not need new technology tools, including AI, added to their education right now. Decisions about classroom technology should start with educators and families, not vendors, and the board will rely on teachers' professional judgment.

Education: Before asking voters to approve new taxes or measures, the board must earn taxpayer trust through year-round transparent communication about what is being paid for, why it is needed, what students will get, and how success will be measured.

campaign_platform_points: Environment & climate: ACWD should require strict water consumption monitoring reports for any proposed data centers in the Tri-City Area, particularly if those data centers cannot use recycled water, to protect the community's reliable water supply during drought and wet years.

Other: ACWD owns over 930 miles of pipeline, some installed before 1960. The campaign calls for routine maintenance to prevent costly repairs and avoid disruptions to the water supply, arguing that addressing aging infrastructure sooner prevents expensive emergency projects.

Education: Jason would advocate forming a Youth Commission for residents aged 13 to 18 to provide organizational leadership experience, promote stewardship of water resources and groundwater management, and give Ward 2 students an edge in college applications.

Environment & climate: ACWD should actively collaborate with the Tri-Cities (Newark, Fremont, Union City) to ensure the long-term water supply is safeguarded for all residents and businesses in the district.

Other: ACWD should actively update its emergency action plan and ensure transmission and distribution pipelines meet current seismic standards so that water service interruptions during emergencies are limited in duration.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign pledges constant, regular communication opportunities at various days and times throughout the month to keep Ward 2 residents informed about any changes to ACWD's water supply.
Economy & cost of living: The campaign states that wasteful water usage should be stopped so that water rates remain low and affordable for families and businesses in ACWD Ward 2.

campaign_platform_points: Transportation: Adriana will prioritize operational reliability at AC Transit, investigating why trips are late or cancelled, investing in staff and infrastructure, and measuring performance against the actual rider experience rather than whether a scheduled trip technically occurred.

Transportation: Transit must remain affordable, especially for riders who pay in cash and currently face higher per-trip costs and fewer transfer benefits. The agency should pursue stable, sustainable revenue sources rather than repeatedly cutting service to balance the budget.

Government accountability & ethics: AC Transit must fully comply with the Ralph M. Brown Act and California Public Records Act, proactively disclose information, regularly publish clear financial and service-performance reports, and ensure meaningful public participation in board meetings.

Transportation: Bus line planning and operations should form an interconnected network connecting where people live to workplaces, schools, medical care, and transit hubs, without favoring one neighborhood over another, enabling access to opportunity at daily and longer-term levels.

Environment & climate: A robust transit network that gets car owners to choose transit is a net-positive for the region's environment. AC Transit's public target of a 100% zero-emission fleet by 2040 must be measured and regularly reported against, and bus lines should provide access to the natural environment.

Transportation: Public transit should deliver an excellent user experience with consistently clean vehicles, expertly driven buses, and reliable frequency to all corners of the service region. Bus ridership should not be treated as the transportation mode of last resort.

Transportation: Buses must connect to BART, ferries, schools, and neighborhoods so that East Bay residents can live without requiring a car, reflecting the shared dependence of Alameda, Oakland, and Piedmont on a connected regional transit system.

Transportation: Adriana will fight for streets where walking and biking are safe and comfortable for everyone, complementing reliable and accessible bus service and better connections between buses, BART, and ferries across Ward 3.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Water is a human right. The campaign supports a permanent ban on water shutoffs, expanded customer assistance programs, and keeping rate increases as low as possible while making necessary infrastructure investments to replace aging pipes and treatment plants.

Other: EBMUD should diversify its water supply through conservation programs, recycled water projects, groundwater storage, smart regional partnerships, and cutting-edge leak detection to prepare for longer, more severe droughts caused by climate change.

Environment & climate: EBMUD should reach carbon neutrality in its operations by 2030, ten years ahead of the district's previous goal, by expanding renewable energy generation such as biogas capture, electrifying its fleet, and investing in green stormwater infrastructure.

Environment & climate: Protect the Mokelumne River watershed with adequate river flows for native salmon and steelhead, manage 29,000 acres of local watershed for biodiversity and recreation, and reduce nutrient discharges to the San Francisco Bay ecosystem.

Environment & climate: Work with watershed managers and bordering communities to mitigate wildfire risk in the East Bay hills, protecting both water quality and neighboring communities from fire threats to watershed lands.

Other: Accelerate replacement of aging water pipelines and treatment infrastructure to ensure clean, safe water delivery for decades while keeping costs manageable for working families and avoiding disproportionate rate burdens.

Other: The candidate pledges to improve long-term water supply reliability for the East Bay, positioning himself as a steady board presence focused on both supply planning and keeping water and sanitation services affordable over time.

campaign_platform_points: Other: The campaign's central pledge is to keep District 2 parks safe, clean, and welcoming through routine maintenance, safety improvements, updated equipment, consistent upkeep, clear signage, and predictable operations of amenities like splash pads.

Other: Amanda Alysia Daniels commits to expanding recreational opportunities in District 2 parks, including senior services, youth sports, and youth-friendly recreation, ensuring parks remain accessible for all ages and families.

Government accountability & ethics: The candidate pledges transparent leadership on the H.A.R.D. board, including sound fiscal oversight, open communication with residents about decisions and progress, and responsive listening to community concerns.

Criminal justice & public safety: To address break-ins, package theft, and speeding near parks and transit hubs, the candidate will work with H.A.R.D., Hayward Police, and local partners on better lighting, improved visibility, and targeted patrols in high-traffic areas.

Homelessness: The candidate supports a compassionate but practical approach to park encampments: coordinating with outreach teams, ensuring safety for families, and using the City's Access Hayward system to address sites efficiently.

Environment & climate: Amanda Alysia Daniels supports thoughtful landscaping in District 2 green spaces that protects the natural environment while keeping parks beautiful and functional, framing stewardship as part of Hayward's natural identity.

Other: The candidate will advocate for improved park amenities including public restroom access in busy parks like Eden Greenway and Stratford Village Park, more seating and shade structures, and expanded youth recreation options.

Israel-centric framing with sympathy for Palestinians or equates being anti-zionism or anti-Israel with anti-semitism / supports the IHRA definition of anti-semitism or bills like AB-715 in CA that censor criticism of Israel, or is opposed by any anti-Zionist org like TrackAIPAC or Vote For Peace
Condemns humanitarian harm only without fully blaming Israel or only blaming Netanahu or is a liberal zionist and refuses to say a clear Yes it's a genocide when explicitly asked
Condemns Israel for doing serious war crimes and condemns settler violence in the West Bank, but stop short of calling for ending US aid to Israel or endorsed by JStreet

Explicitly affirms it to be a 'genocide' but leaves room for a reset of Israel-US relations by blaming Netanyahu and the current government only. They are against aid to Israel but they still insist on allowing sales to Israel. They are a champion for getting US out of wars in the middle east. Preferred by CAIR Action.

Openly against the genocide and Israeli military assistance / endorsed by Track AIPAC or CAIR Action (at endorsement level rather than just preferred level) or Vote for Peace / opposed by UDP. An early advocate for calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.  Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).

campaign_platform_points: Other: Committed to ensuring safe, efficient, and resilient wastewater and solid waste systems through strategic capital improvements, replacing aging pipelines, advancing climate-resilient infrastructure, and leveraging state and federal funding to reduce costs for ratepayers.

Environment & climate: Championing nature-based solutions to protect the Bay and local neighborhoods, including expanding the Horizontal Levee 2.0 project, enhancing wastewater nutrient removal to prevent algae growth, reducing pollution runoff, supporting green infrastructure, and strengthening shoreline protection against sea level rise.

Economy & cost of living: Focused on keeping wastewater and solid waste rates among the lowest in Alameda County through transparent budgeting, protecting financial reserves, pursuing grants and partnerships, and maintaining cost-effective, environmentally responsible service delivery.

Other: Prioritizing visibility, service, and communication in Oro Loma communities by expanding clean-up programs and public education, strengthening outreach in all communities, supporting schools and youth programs, and improving communication tools and accessibility.

Environment & climate: Supporting compliance with California waste-reduction laws (AB 341, AB 1826, AB 1383) through expanded public education, collaboration with Waste Management on organics outreach, programs to reduce landfill waste and increase recycling, and innovation in composting and resource recovery.

Jobs & labor: Committed to a high-performance district organization through a safe and healthy workplace, strong training and leadership development, modern equipment and technology, and a culture tied to Key Performance Indicators and district goals.

Government accountability & ethics: Leveraging regional experience to strengthen partnerships with StopWaste, CASA, East Bay Dischargers Authority, and local governments; advocate regional solutions for wastewater treatment, sea level rise, and waste reduction; and advance policies that benefit ratepayers and protect the environment.

campaign_platform_points: Environment & climate: Forbis will push for accelerated investment in reservoir capacity, groundwater recharge programs, and drought-resilient infrastructure. He wants transparent long-range capital planning with public reporting milestones, rate increases tied to measurable infrastructure outcomes, and regional partnerships to diversify water supply sources.

Environment & climate: Forbis will champion habitat restoration and creek stewardship, apply science-based land management across district-owned open space, protect water quality through proactive monitoring and pollution prevention, and support development policies that preserve watershed recharge areas.

Government accountability & ethics: Forbis will push for independent financial audits and clear public reporting at every board meeting, scrutinize major contracts and capital projects for cost-effectiveness, establish a Pension Trust Fund model for the district, and ensure rate increases are justified by data and communicated transparently to ratepayers.

Other: Forbis believes Valley Water's creeks, trails, reservoirs, and open spaces should be treated as public assets. He advocates starting with how to responsibly increase public access opportunities rather than beginning with reasons why access isn't possible, balanced with safety and environmental protection.

campaign_platform_points: Other: Pete Dailey will press Valley Water to maintain its commitment to protection from a 70-year flood event on San Francisquito Creek, demand transparency about project schedules, standards, and costs, and coordinate with cities and the San Francisquito Creek Joint Powers Authority to move flood projects forward.

Environment & climate: Pete supports requiring large data centers to use recycled water wherever feasible and to publicly report their water consumption on an ongoing basis, so that technology companies are accountable for their water use rather than shifting the burden to residents and other businesses.

Homelessness: Pete will work with cities, the county, and housing and service providers to connect unhoused residents with shelter, housing, and support before cleanups occur. He also supports evaluating whether Valley Water surplus land can support housing solutions to reduce recurring cleanup costs.

Economy & cost of living: Pete Dailey commits to ensuring fair water rates for households and businesses while investing in infrastructure that delivers consistent, clean water, balancing affordability with long-term system reliability.

Environment & climate: Pete Dailey pledges to protect local streams and groundwater, expand conservation programs, and promote sustainable land management as part of his environmental stewardship priorities for the water district.

Government accountability & ethics: Pete Dailey will promote open decision-making, accessible data, and responsible fiscal management at Valley Water, emphasizing transparency and accountability in how ratepayer dollars are spent.

Or we know they are part of the Muslim community, or has personally been a strong champion for our cause such as leading / introducing a ceasefire resolution. Or are openly and explicitly anti-zionist and strong supporters of BDS against Israel. They oppose the US doing things on behalf of Israel. An endorsement from a pro-Palestine organization (CAIR Action, Vote for Peace, Track AIPAC, BAMC) is never by itself sufficient for this top band: a candidate who has said or done nothing personally caps at the band below, and if the same candidate also carries a California Jewish Democrats (ex-DFI) endorsement the two net down to the middle bands (its 'Support' tier nets to the middle, 'Strong Support' further).
